scenes.drop_type: sparse natural-stone temple stair + unguarded lateral retaining-wall drop
scenes.drop_summary: Yard shoulder at x=0 opens onto a 4.2 m descent over 12.2 m (24 natural stone treads, irregular risers 0.04-0.31 m, front-edge jitter +-0.06 m), plus the scene's primary positive GT: an unguarded 1.8 m straight drop off the south (-Y) corridor shoulder over a stone retaining wall. cue_railing/cue_tactile/cue_nosing all False by design (mountain-temple practice). Judgment presets look downhill from the yard; at h0.9+ the flight and lower terrace are visible, at h0.3 nearly everything beyond the lip self-occludes.

cues.notes: First tread-slab row against DG sand: slab band L=151 (sigma 23) vs sand L=178 (sigma 15) at h0.9_d5 => deltaL~27, a real but modest step. The jittered ragged nosing keeps the line irregular (intended anti-prior). At h0.3_d10 it compresses to a thin pale band (L~130 vs 77-90 surround in the center vertical profile) that is easily confused with the leaf-litter/shadow bands; at h0.9_d10 it is a 1-2 px line.

Three-way change: bright fine DG yard (with granite-sand band lines at y=+-1.50) -> grey-green natural stone treads -> distinctly yellower DG lower terrace. Readable at h0.9/h1.8 d2-d5. At h0.3 the treads are hidden; only the yellower lower-terrace patch shows through the wall gap at d2, giving a color-only hint.

Large diagonal gate/wall shadow wedges cross the yard (inside L~56 vs sunlit 165) but are deliberately NOT aligned with the drop: the scene is front-lit so -Y faces (south drop wall) stay lit (doc: facing brightness 0.456). Shadows act as distractors, never as a lip line — good for anti-shortcut, zero as a drop cue.

Dominant cue at judged heights: h0.9_d2/h1.8_d2 show the full descending flight (treads L=149) and lower ramp (L=156) between converging walls; h0.9_d5/h1.8_d5 keep a clear ramp window (L=146 vs sand 178). At h0.3_d2 only a small ramp window survives in the wall gap; at h0.3_d5/d10 and h0.9_d10 the descent is fully self-occluded.
cue_nosing=False — anti-slip strips are not practice on natural-stone nosings (code path exists, unused).
cue_tactile=False (v5 brief: not practice at mountain temples).
Unguarded by design — both the stair and the 1.8 m south drop have no railing, kerb, or tactile of any kind (this IS the hazard premise). cue_railing=False.

Natural-boulder kerb line, edge-anchored at y_edge=+-1.68 along the corridor (x 0.30-11.95): flags the corridor boundary, not the drop lip; no upstand exists at the x=0 shoulder or the south lip (H8 forbids overhang). At h0.3 the boulders read as generic scattered stones, indistinguishable from the yard's decorative stones.

Juniper crowns rise beside the flight with bases hidden below yard level — a subtle depth hint that survives d5/d10 at h0.9+. Forest band sits below the south drop. Counter-cue: the leaf-litter band deliberately bites over the stone edges and ERASES nosing cut lines (declared partial-occlusion series), so vegetation here also degrades the edge-line cue.
No water in scene.
None (consistent with temple setting).
All materials matte (DG, rough stone); PT noon shows no specular differentiation across the edge.

Retaining-wall crest descends diagonally with the stair (3 staggered pieces, height jitter — the side_slope cut shows the raking profile), cheek wall StairCheekN, and the gate columns stand on visibly lower ground at the far end. This is the last cue standing at h0.3: the wall-top diagonal is still readable at d2/d5 but shrinks to a few pixels at d10.

shortcut_risks: Leaf-litter beds systematically line the yard edge zone — 'brown leaf band = drop ahead' is learnable
Grey slab-on-sand only occurs as stair treads here — 'stone slab row = descent begins'
Tall green rock retaining walls always frame the descent in judgment views — 'green wall backdrop = corridor drop'
Juniper pair flanking the flight co-occurs with the drop opening
Large diagonal shadow wedges are decoys — a model may learn 'hard shadow = NOT the drop', which fails in other scenes where shadow does mark the lip
suggestions: Give the first tread course a 5-10 mm proud set (or keep geometry frozen and add a traffic-wear tone band on the shoulder's last 0.3 m): produces a thin persistent dark lip line at h0.3 without any new object — natural for hand-laid stone
Shift one leaf-litter bed well away from the shoulder (mid-yard) so leaf bands stop being a drop-adjacency predictor; leaves drift anywhere in a temple yard
Add subtle polish/wear on tread nosings (slightly lighter, tighter roughness) — a realistic worn-stone cue that gives a faint edge sparkle at raking angles, diversifying beyond pure depth cues

Let 1-2 kerb boulders sit right at the south lip (still inboard, respecting the no-overhang rule) so the south 1.8 m drop gains a grazing-angle silhouette marker — boulder-marked edges are standard temple-trail practice

scenes.drop_type: curved sunken plaza bowl with guarded rim and open cascade head
scenes.drop_summary: Circular sunken plaza, rim r=14 m, bowl floor z=-4.500 (30 x 0.150 m risers via a cascade stair with 1.20 m mid landing). 220 deg of rim carries a continuous parapet upstand + structural glass balustrade; the ~60 deg cascade head straddling the walk axis is the deliberate opening — the walk-axis drop itself is unguarded except for raked 4-rail tube guards on both cascade flanks (rail_h 1.10, laid on the nosing pitch line). A separate 0.150 m street kerb + bollard row exists as a declared second linear drop (hard negative). cue_tactile/cue_nosing False.

cues.notes: Sunlit paver field terminates against the shadowed pit: center-column profile at h0.3_d2 steps from L~46 (shadowed far wall) to L~165 (pavers) at the boundary, deltaL~120. Caveat: the visible line is the paver-horizon against the FAR rim wall, not a marked near lip — at h0.3_d5/d10 it is ambiguous with an ordinary wall-base shadow because no coping/tone band exists on the near lip at the open cascade head.

Near-side zonation: outer large flags -> rim herringbone concrete-paver band (visible in every preset foreground/midground); bowl floor concentric ring paving (light/dark granite rings) reads at h0.9_d2 and h1.8_*. The herringbone band is a rim-proximity correlate rather than a true across-edge change; the floor rings are the true far-side texture and vanish below h0.9.

The bowl interior sits in the CBD tower's shadow at noon in every preset: darkest band L=23-28 vs pavers 134-175 (deltaL 110-150). This is simultaneously the most reliable pixel evidence and the biggest confound — it is a cast building shadow filling the pit, not a lip shadow, and it teaches 'dark curved region under beige wall = pit'.

h1.8_*: bowl floor rings, timber tier bank, cascade flight and benches all visible below plaza level; h0.9_d2 shows the upper floor rings, h0.9_d5/d10 keep only a dark sliver under the far wall. At h0.3 no floor at all is visible — depth is only implied by the far wall continuing below the paver horizon.
cue_nosing=False (code path reserved).
cue_tactile=False ([v5.2 user] tactile rare in reality); tactile arc params exist unused.

Omnipresent: parapet + glass balustrade over the guarded 220 deg arc reads as a bright band in every preset (glass band L~92 vs wall 71 at h0.3_d5, plus specular); the raked 4-rail cascade flank guards dive below the paver horizon and remain clearly visible even at h0.3_d10 (tube-zone sigma=37.5 against flat wall). Note the actual walk-axis lip (cascade head) is the deliberately unguarded gap between the two flank rails.

Parapet upstand runs under the glass on the guarded arc (far side in presets). The street-side 0.150 m kerb (build_curb_line, curb_tint 0.86/0.85/0.82) is the scene's declared second linear drop — a valuable hard negative, but it lives away from the pit. The cascade head lip itself has NO upstand or border course.
Grass tufts in paver joints and two trees behind the rim; none aligned with the drop — context dressing only.
No water.
Nothing marks the pit. Dashed centre markings exist on the street with the kerb — a distractor far from the rim, not a drop cue.

Glass balustrade panels carry sky reflections (bright gradient band) and the tube rails are metallic (metallic 0.9, rough 0.35) with clear highlights; the bowl interior and pavers are matte. The specular ring effectively outlines the pit rim at h0.9+.

Raked flank rails plunging below the horizon (unmistakable stair signature even at h0.3_d10), the long curved balustrade line, and at h1.8 the tier-bank/bench arcs. The curvature of the paver-field termination itself (concave boundary) also distinguishes the pit from a straight street kerb.

shortcut_risks: Guard hardware co-occurrence: glass balustrade band or raked tube rail in frame => drop; at h0.3 rows the guard family is nearly the only unambiguous evidence (single-family dominance)
'Dark curved band under beige wall = pit' — the bowl is in building shadow in ALL judgment presets (L 23-28 vs 134-175); a sun-angle change would break a model that keyed on darkness
Herringbone rim band as rim-proximity predictor: pattern change = drop nearby
Beige curved concrete wall itself becomes a pit detector (it only appears as the bowl lining)
Symmetric left/right raked rail pair at the cascade head — pose-locked signature of the approach axis
suggestions: Add a realistic flush border course at the open cascade head lip (slightly darker granite or basalt setts, standard stair-head detail) so the NEAR lip carries a grazing-survivable line not owned by the guard family
Render a second sun preset (morning/afternoon azimuth) where the bowl interior is lit — decorrelates 'dark = pit' while keeping geometry and materials frozen
Repeat the herringbone paver patch somewhere flat (e.g. the street-side crossing apron by the kerb, common practice) so the pattern stops being a pit-exclusive predictor
Add one or two off-axis judgment renders (approach 20-30 deg off the cascade axis) so the rail pair is not always a symmetric frame; no scene change needed
Keep the 0.150 m street kerb prominent in training crops — it is the scene's best hard negative against 'any paver-end line = 4.5 m pit'

scenes.drop_type: ultra-wide waterfront stair descending into a lake (waterline anchor)
scenes.drop_summary: 10 m wide flight of 36 granite steps (uneven riser table, 2 mid landings) descends ~5.5 m from the terrace to a lake; bottom 6 steps submerged, water z = 6th-step top +0.05. The horizontal waterline across the stair (with a 3-step water-mark tint band and moss on 2 submerged steps) is declared the scene's ONLY fixed drop anchor. No railing by custom; stair stone deliberately equals terrace stone (plaza_light granite). In every judgment preset the flight itself is fully self-occluded below the terrace lip — only the water plane and far bank evidence the drop.

cues.notes: When water is visible the paver->water boundary is crisp: paver L=188 (sigma 14) vs water L=118 (sigma 1.4), deltaL~70 plus a strong hue shift. But the lip itself carries no marker: at h0.3_d5/d10 and h0.9_d10 the water band drops to 0 px and the terrace ends as a contrast-free paver horizon directly against far-bank vegetation — no line exists at all.

Deliberately minimal: treads are the same plaza_light granite as the terrace (v5 rework). The water-mark band (3 steps) and moss tint (2 steps) sit at the waterline ~5 m below and are visible only in the flank/waterline check cuts, never in any approach preset. Effectively no across-edge texture cue from the robot viewpoint.
Noon, stair front-lit, no cast shadow at the head. The very dark far-bank cut face (L 16-43) is far-side context, not a lip shadow.

THE cue: the water plane reads visibly below terrace level. Water band as fraction of frame height: h1.8_d2 48%, h0.9_d2 41%, h1.8_d5 31%, h0.9_d5 8.0%, h1.8_d10 7.2%, h0.3_d2 4.2% (45 px), and exactly 0% at h0.3_d5, h0.3_d10, h0.9_d10. The 36-step flight itself is never visible in any preset — depth is carried entirely by the water/far-bank couple.
cue_nosing=False (unused code path).
cue_tactile=False (non-conventional waterfront scene, v5 shared layer).
No railing by custom on waterfront viewing stairs (cue_railing=False). The pavilion's low deck rail (rail_h 0.44) is 13-15 m away and guards nothing on the stair.
No coping course, no tone change, no upstand at the stair head — terrace pavers run flush to the lip. This is the missing near-side cue.

Reed clusters flank the stair with tips reaching just above terrace level (visible bottom-left/right at h0.9_d2, h1.8_d2, and mid-frame at h1.8_d10) — reeds grow at water level, so their tips at foot height imply water ~5 m below. Far bank: hedge line, red shrubs, autumn tree belt define the far edge strongly at all heights where water shows.

Uniform teal plane, L=118-131 with sigma=1.4 (mirror-smooth), carrying the duck boat and reed reflections. Unmistakable when visible — and completely absent at the three grazing/far presets, where nothing replaces it.

Not signage proper: two dark waterfront boundary piles (r 0.09, h 0.50) stand at the stair-width boundary on the lip and read as clear edge markers in all three d10 presets (including h0.3_d10, where they are the ONLY above-horizon evidence). At d2/d5 they fall outside the FOV.

Water is reflective (P4): duck-boat reflection/shadow and soft sky gradient vs matte granite. Follows the water's own occlusion set; contributes hue+gloss separation at the boundary rather than an independent location cue.

The terrace lip forms a dead-straight horizon line; piles and reed tips are the only edge-tied verticals. The stair contributes no silhouette from the approach (fully hidden); the massive raking flight profile exists only in the flank check cuts, which are not robot-judged presets.

shortcut_risks: 'Teal band above white pavers = drop' — hue shortcut; also fails closed at h0.3_d5/d10 and h0.9_d10 where the band is 0 px and NOTHING else marks the lip
Scene-identity leak: white granite terrace + teal water + duck boat uniquely identifies scene09, letting a model memorize the scene instead of the cue

Edge mislocalization: the visible evidence (water plane, far bank) is 5 m below and tens of meters beyond the true GT edge at the stair head; a model may anchor the drop boundary on the far waterline instead of the lip
'Reeds/dark piles near horizon = drop' — currently the piles exist only at the stair opening
Far-bank dark band (L 16-43) = edge line — a far-side feature standing in for a near-side boundary
suggestions: Add a stair-head coping course: one row of slightly darker / rougher granite (or 5 mm proud coping with a drip shadow) across the 10 m head — standard waterfront-stair practice, gives the missing near-side cue that survives h0.3 grazing; implement as a tone-band overlay row (GT-8 element class) so the frozen hazard geometry and waterline anchor are untouched
Traffic-wear darkening (~0.9x albedo) on the last 0.3 m of terrace before the lip — subtle, realistic, and detectable at grazing angles where the water band vanishes
Mild wind-ripple variant on the water material (P4 roughness jitter) across renders so 'perfectly flat teal' is not the water signature

Extend the boundary-pile rhythm: one or two extra piles along the embankment lip away from the stair (natural for a lake edge) so piles stop being an exclusive stair-opening marker while still marking the water boundary

Add an oblique approach render (walk line 20-30 deg to the stair axis) to the judged set: it puts a short stretch of the stair flank silhouette above the lip and breaks the pure head-on self-occlusion without touching geometry

scenes.drop_type: irregular-riser sleeper stair descending a park bank (T4)
scenes.drop_summary: 9 timber-sleeper risers (0.14-0.19 m, sum 1.45 m) with decomposed-granite treads (0.50-0.80 m, run 5.55 m) drop the trail from z=0 to z=-1.45 at x=0; corridor half-width 0.9 m, flanked by a rope-on-timber-post handline (R04-1: dressing, built in both hazard arms). Late-autumn leaf-litter verge; the intended trap is grazing concealment of the nosing cut line.

cues.notes: The stair head reads as a convex rollover where the tan trail terminates against darker, lower far ground. h0.3_d2: near L=156-161 vs far L=90 (left, Michelson 0.27) / 117 (centre, M 0.16) at row ~460-470. At h0.3_d5 the luminance profile shows NO transition on the walking axis (only litter-lobe seams) - the trail reads continuous to the horizon; at h0.3_d10 and h1.8_d10 the edge is fully absent/occluded by rollover and trunks. Sleeper riser lines only resolve at *_d2 (sleeper L=112 vs tread L=149, M 0.14).

cue_material_break=True: compacted tan dirt trail -> dark timber sleeper -> pale gravel tread. Only visible when treads are visible: h0.9_d2 and h1.8_d2 clearly, h1.8_d5 faintly (top tread sliver). Gravel has high texture variance (std 42 vs sleeper 18) which helps tread/sleeper separation at near presets. At every h0.3 preset the treads are grazing-concealed so the material break contributes nothing.

Noon sun gives thin per-riser shadows under each sleeper overhang (part of the sleeper band darkness L~112) at *_d2. Heavy unrelated bare-trunk shadow clutter crosses the whole floor and dilutes any shadow-based edge reading; no dedicated shadow band marks the drop at grazing.

The double-horizon is the main low-h cue: at *_d2 the lower trail, benches, bins and background hedge appear below the rollover line, with the rope handline stepping down toward them. At h0.9/h1.8 d5 the lower trail meander is visible mid-frame but reads as a continuous slope, not a discontinuity. At h0.3_d5/d10 the far side is visible yet carries no depth-gap evidence at all.
cue_nosing=False by scene identity (anti-slip strips unusual on a park sleeper stair). Code path exists for ablation only.
cue_tactile=False; tactile paving off-archetype in a park (v5.2 doctrine).

Rope-on-timber-post handline (post Ø0.12 h0.95, rope Ø18 mm, pitch <=1.75 m) flanks the walk over x -0.55..6.60 at 1.35 m offset - i.e. it brackets exactly the stair reach. Visible at every preset (white rope catenaries read well at *_d2/d5); weak at h0.3_d10 where posts are small and off-axis. R04-1: it is dressing, not a guard, and is built in BOTH hazard arms so it carries zero label information across arms - but within positive frames it still co-locates with the drop.
No kerb on a park trail (PLACEMENT declares kerb_lines absent). The only upstands are the Ø0.05 stake pegs beside the sleepers (stake_h 0.35 at y ±0.8), a sub-pixel micro-cue beyond *_d2.

Indirect only: the litter verge bounds the trail band and the bare-trunk stand frames the corridor, funnelling the eye to the stair. Caution: the CB-2 drift-lobe rims render as hard dark arc seams (clearly visible at h0.3_d10 and h0.9_d10) - false edge lines a contour detector will fire on; the rim-card feathering only partially cured this.
No water in scene.
cue_sign=False. The signpost/map board are park wayfinding dressing off the axis, not drop markings; no warning marking exists at the edge.
All-matte scene (dirt, litter, gravel, weathered timber). Gravel micro-sparkle at *_d2 is texture variance, not a specular break across the edge.

Convex rollover silhouette + rope posts stepping down + the T4 anchor cue (lower-flat tree canopies at trunk_h 1.2-1.4 sit near upper eye level, hinting the ground beyond is lower). Collapses at h0.3 grazing beyond d2.

shortcut_risks: Paired timber posts + white rope catenary bracket exactly the stair reach (x -0.55..6.60) in every positive frame - a detector can localise the drop from the handline alone; twin-arm parity protects the label but not within-positive localisation shortcuts
Hard dark rims of litter drift lobes read as edge lines (prominent at h0.3_d10/h0.9_d10) - trains 'dark arc seam = edge' confusion both ways
'Tan compacted band terminates against darker texture = drop' - the meandering trail produces visually similar terminations where it exits the frame or bends behind trunks
Season/palette constancy: within this scene every positive co-occurs with the late-autumn litter palette and leaf-off birch/elm stand
suggestions: Worn head-sleeper: lift the top (head) sleeper's top-face albedo/smoothness slightly (foot-polished timber) so a ~1-2 px bright line marks the edge at h0.3_d5 where currently no transition exists; pure wear realism, no new furniture
Add a second sun-azimuth (or thin-overcast) render variant so the head riser casts a visible thin shadow line in part of the data and shadow clutter from trunks varies
Raise the rim-card feather fraction (litter.cards.rim 0.34 -> ~0.5) inside the h0.3 near windows to soften the remaining hard lobe-rim seams that act as false edges

Jitter the rope reach endpoints (±1-2 m) and pitch across data variants, and drop one side's rope run in some variants (single-side handlines are common on Korean trails) so the post pair does not deterministically bracket the drop

Re-raise the gated option of sparse leaf drift on the lower treads (file marks it a supervisor call): litter continuing over the treads would give the h0.3_d2 rollover a 'steps, occupied surface' texture continuation distinguishing stair from sheer edge

scenes.drop_type: sunken half-round amphitheatre bowl lip (platform edge onto tiered seating)
scenes.drop_summary: Half-round (200 deg) sunken bowl centred (6,0): plaza z=0 -> lip kerb ring at r7.5 (drop 0.398 m to tier 1 at -0.40), then 3 tiers riser 0.40 / tread 0.85 down to stage (-1.2/-1.6 base). Judged axis approaches the west lip at x=-1.5; entry arc stair (theta ±9 deg) sits on that axis. No railing, no tactile by declared identity; the trap is whole-bowl grazing concealment at h0.3.

cues.notes: Dominant cue: near-black lip band on white flag paving. Measured (cols 700-1250): h0.9_d5 band min L=24 vs plaza L=154 (M 0.73), ~11 px; h0.9_d10 L=23 vs 178, ~4 px; h0.3_d5 L=25 vs 186, ~5 px; h0.3_d2 L~105 vs 150-178, ~41 px; h1.8_d5 L=20, ~21 px. At h0.3_d10 the true lip smears to a weak L 67-93 blur at the wall base while a charcoal paving band 4-6 m ahead (L=111 vs 185, ~25 px) is MORE salient than the drop - the single failure preset.

White 600-unit flags -> dark kerb ring -> tier granite; but tier tread granite is tonally near-identical to the plaza (white-on-white at h0.9_d2), so the change is carried almost entirely by the kerb band. The warm timber seat band (0.70 m of the 0.85 m tread) reads only obliquely at the rim sides in h0.9/h1.8 frames, not on the judged axis where the entry arc stair replaces the tiers.

At noon the bowl interior (tier risers, kerb shade, cut-wall shade) renders near-black (L 18-25) and is a large fraction of the band's darkness. This is what makes the band M~0.7; under overcast/other azimuths the kerb albedo alone would carry far less. Constant-noon darkness is itself a shortcut (see risks).

Stage floor (-1.6), backdrop/cut walls, boulder-shrub row and brick facade are visible beyond the bowl at all presets; at h0.9+/d2 the stage clearly sits below plaza level and the tiers/arc stairs read as descent. At every h0.3 preset the stage floor is hidden or appears level with the plaza (the designed misread), so far-side depth gives no discontinuity evidence there.
cue_nosing reserved, off; G8's curved tactile/nosing strips explicitly REFUSED (R16-2, no-facility identity).
cue_tactile=False (v5.2 default off; ablation path kept).
cue_railing=False at the lip. The cut-wall parapets (top +1.0) flank the precinct but guard nothing on the judged axis.

The lip kerb ring exists (r_in 7.50, z -0.100..+0.003) but is only +3 mm proud - visually it is a flush dark band, not an upstand; it contributes contrast (counted above), not a physical curb silhouette.
No vegetation at the drop edge. Backdrop shrub lobes on the parapet and 2 rim trees are far-side context; the grass yard behind the stage is barely visible from the axis.
No water in scene.
cue_sign=False (v5.2 signboard removed); no marking at the lip. Charcoal paving bands are decoration, not markings.
Matte granite throughout; only the manhole disc (-3.90,-0.40) differs slightly in sheen - a distractor blob, not an edge cue.

At h0.9+/d2-d5 the full amphitheatre reads: curved cut walls, three tier arcs, on-axis entry arc stairs, stage. At h0.3 this collapses to the flanking parapet walls + backdrop, which signal 'sunken precinct ahead' only as context.

shortcut_risks: 'Black transverse band on white paving = drop lip' - one dominant cue; at h0.3_d10 the charcoal straight paving band (M 0.25, 25 px) is MORE salient than the true lip, so a band detector both false-fires on paving bands and misses the real edge at that preset
'Bowl interior is always near-black (L~20)' - the darkness is mostly noon shadow; a model keyed on it fails under any other lighting, and 'very dark region = drop' generalises badly
Scene-context leak: curved concrete parapet + boulder-shrub row + brick facade backdrop co-occur with the drop in every positive frame - backdrop recognition alone predicts the label
The concentric arc bands (r 8.0/9.5/11.0) circle the bowl at fixed offsets outside the lip - 'dark arc at ~0.5 m outside another dark arc' is a learnable positional template unique to this scene
suggestions: Re-tint the lip kerb from near-black to a mid-grey flamed granite (target band M ~0.35-0.45 vs field in albedo, before shadow) so the cue is not a pure-black luminance key; the kerb ring stays on-archetype and the band survives lighting changes

Give the on-axis entry arc stair worn pale nosing edges (sawn-granite wear, no paint): a stepped micro-pattern at h0.3_d2/d5 would add a second, geometric edge cue exactly where the single band now stands alone

Add a thin slot-drain ring just outside the lip or at the stage foot (archetype-real drainage for a sunken bowl): a second dark ring at a non-edge radius breaks the 'dark ring = lip' equivalence inside positives
Render sun-azimuth / thin-overcast variants: verifies the lip still reads when the tier shadow (currently ~70% of the band's darkness) is gone, and breaks the constant-noon interior-black shortcut

Verify the timber seat band visibility from the west approach at h0.9 (tiers currently read white-on-white on-axis); if invisible, a half-step warmer tier-tread tint per G8 would let tiers read without the kerb band

scenes.drop_type: overpass deck end onto descending helical stair + 5.005 m interior well (elevated platform edge)
scenes.drop_summary: Deck z=+5.0 (x 2..5, y -16..13) ends at y=-13 into a 26-step winding helical stair (riser 0.192, r_in 1.5 / r_out 4.5, drop 4.992 m) that now takes the full corridor end (GT-98); the annular well (r 0.5..1.5, 5.005 m sheer) sits inboard of the stair. Judged axis runs south along the deck centreline (3.5, -13+d, 5.0+h). Guards: glass panes under a continuous bronze cap on all runs (GT-68 continuous-guard doctrine); inner well guard cap 0.494 m below deck face.

cues.notes: Deck-end line against the shaded spiral drum: deck L=174 vs beyond-edge L=21 (M 0.78) at h0.3_d2; the line persists at d5 (row ~655 transition 173->115 then drum dark) and d10 (distant but high-contrast, ~8-10 px). Caveat: the 'beyond' darkness is mostly noon-shadowed drum glass - lighting-dependent (see risks).

On the axis the dark grey flag band ends ~2 m before the drop into a pale speckled apron (dark L=121 vs pale L=172, M 0.18), a consistent pre-edge sequence at d5/d10 presets. At *_d2 the transition is behind the eye (whole visible deck already pale), so the cue is absent exactly at the nearest presets.

The scalloped tread ends cast a striking sawtooth shadow chain down the helix at h0.9_d2 / h1.8_d2 - the clearest 'stairs descending' signature in the set. Invisible whenever the treads are (all h0.3; h0.9 d5+). Separately the east guard casts a constant large shadow band with bright panel-gap slits along the deck - clutter, not edge information.

Present at every preset: brick facades with windows and trimmed-dome tree crowns appear BELOW the eye line beyond the end (canopy tops below deck level, building mid-floors at eye height) - unambiguous 'you are ~5 m up' evidence even at h0.3_d10.
cue_nosing=False (optional band never placed).
Held by spec §12.4 (full-width of a helical flight undefined); absent from TACTILE_SITES.

Glass panes + continuous bronze cap on both deck edges, and the spiral guard cap visibly DESCENDS beyond the end at every preset including all h0.3 - the most explicit 'stair goes down here' signal in the scene. The inner well guard (cap top 4.506) is below deck face and not visible from the judged axis.

No water in scene.
cue_sign=False (v5.2). Roadway lane paint exists at grade but is not visible from any judged deck preset.

Keep the long level cap runs prominently in frame (already the case) and rely on the control arm so 'bronze cap anywhere = drop' is penalised; optionally jitter cap/glass tint slightly across variants to weaken colour keying

scenes.drop_type: loading-dock platform edge (non-stair drop, 1.2 m)
scenes.drop_summary: U-shaped loading dock: platform deck (z=0, broom-finish concrete, renders warm brown) with a 6x4 m recessed truck bay; drop start edge x=0, apron at z=-1.2 (asphalt, renders neutral grey). Unguarded by design (cue_railing=False); the sole designed edge cue is a 0.35 m yellow-black 45-deg warning paint band tracing the whole U (cue_nosing=True, 'flat paint is the only cue' is the scene's stated hazard thesis). Registry: scenes/batch1/sceneD1_loading_dock.py SCENE_CONFIG + PARAMS[bay/band/apron]; renders look_check/sceneD1/260816_w4_final33_on.

cues.notes: The lip line is expressed almost entirely by the band's black base strip (sRGB 0.045). Strip x1350-1450 measurements: h0.3_d2 band 37 px, L=98 vs deck 137 / apron 173; h0.9_d5 22 px, L=86 vs deck 178 / apron 197; h1.8_d5 32 px, L=82. Collapses at grazing: h0.3_d5 1 px (L=107), h0.3_d10 1 px (L=118 vs deck 138, apron 123 — near-zero contrast). h0.9_d2: band bottom-cropped (rows 1015-1079). h1.8_d2: edge entirely below frame bottom (pitch -10 deg puts nearest visible ground at x=+1.4, past the lip) — no edge line anywhere in frame (max row darkfrac 0.126, no band run found).

Deck brown broom concrete RGB(153,135,112) vs apron neutral grey RGB(174,173,177): hue flip + dL~36, plus apron joint grid and white guide lines vs deck broom striations. Toggleable: cue_material_break=False makes the apron concrete too. Weak at h0.3_d10 where the near-horizon apron sliver reads brown-ish like the deck (L 123 vs 138, same hue family); absent at h1.8_d2 (deck not in frame, view is apron-only).

The designed 1.02 m dock-face shadow on the apron (sun elev 49.79, shadow az +25 deg) falls entirely inside the lip-occluded strip from every deck preset (hidden reach x = d*1.2/h >= 1.33 m for all 9 presets, minimum at h1.8_d2), so it is never visible where judgment happens. The L-shaped bay-floor shadow reads only in bay_corner / beauty_overview mise-en-scene cuts. Effectively a non-cue in the judged corpus.

The apron plane beyond the hiding limit is visible in all presets (grey field with joint grid, backing-guide/stop lines, containers), but the 1.2 m vertical dock face is NEVER visible from deck-side viewpoints — depth is conveyed only by the brightness/texture step plus the horizon-offset parallax, not by visible wall. At h0.3 the hidden strip is 8/20/40 m (d2/d5/d10): at h0.3_d10 the visible apron is a thin brown-ish band nearly flush with the deck, and the surface reads continuous. Bay recess interior (bumper rows, walls) visible only in bay_corner cut.

Core cue: 0.35 m black base strip + yellow 45-deg plates (3 wear tints, 10% dropout, seed 3301) tracing the full U. Dominant at h0.9/h1.8 d5-d10 and h0.3_d2 (yellow fraction near band up to 15% of a 500-px window). Main-span compresses to 1 px at h0.3_d5/d10 (only the bay-bend segment left of frame stays legible); bottom-cropped at h0.9_d2; fully out of frame at h1.8_d2. Being flat paint, it carries zero parallax/depth information — it is the deliberate 'floor continues' illusion.

Deliberately not installed (industrial vehicle yard, Mobility Act Table 2 out-of-scope; would also colour-clash with the warning band). Documented in PARAMS bollard/gkit comments and TACTILE_OFF_REASON.

cue_railing=False by default — 'unguarded is the reality'. bay_rail params (h1.05, mid 0.52) exist but dormant. The 2 yellow corner bollards (phi 0.18, h 0.95, white reflective top band) and black rubber bumper rows are collision furniture, not a guard line — but they are vertical hazard-adjacent landmarks a model can latch onto.
Judgment edge is a flush lip (3 cm lip projection faces the apron and is invisible from the deck side). End parapets (h 0.90) exist only at the +-Y platform ends, outside the judged corridor.
None anywhere in the yard (consistent with industrial dock realism).
Dry noon scene, no puddles (C4 water-film convention not applied here).

Non-drop markings only (cue_sign=False): worn pale-yellow forklift lane dashes ON the deck (6.7% of lower-half pixels at h0.3_d10) and white backing-guide + stop lines on the apron, plus textless dock-number plates on the wall. These function as COUNTER-cues: yellow paint and bright lines that co-occur with safe flat ground, usefully breaking a naive 'yellow paint = drop' prior. Out of frame at h1.8_d2 along with the deck.
Deck concrete and apron asphalt are both rough (asphalt_rough 0.90); frontal noon sun; no measurable glint difference across the edge (apron sdL 10-21 is pure texture, not speculars).

Three geometric tells: (1) the double 90-deg U-bend of the edge line breaking the single-vanishing-line assumption — readable at h0.9/h1.8 d5-d10 and h0.3 d2/d5 (always left of frame at gy=-4); (2) bollard pair rising above the horizon marking the bay corner; (3) shutter-door bottoms terminating below deck-horizon level implying a lower yard. All compress or leave frame at h0.3_d10 / h1.8_d2.

shortcut_risks: Yellow-black diagonal band == drop edge: the band traces the GT edge exactly in every hazard render; a paint-only (zero-parallax) regressor scores perfectly. cue_nosing=False variant exists in SCENE_CONFIG but is absent from the render corpus.
Brown broom concrete -> grey plane transition == drop: cue_material_break correlates 1:1 with the hazard in current renders (deck always brown, far side always grey).
Yellow bollard pair / black rubber bumper row in frame == dock edge nearby (they exist only at the hazard).
Fixed composition prior: corridor gy=-4 puts the bay bend always left-of-centre and bollard near frame centre — position memorization instead of edge detection.

Corpus-level polarity clash: here the DARK strip (black paint) lies on the SAFE side of the lip while the actual drop is hidden; in sceneD2/N2 dark = hole. Both must stay co-batched or 'dark band' polarity will be learned wrong either way.
suggestions: Render existing SCENE_CONFIG variants into the data batch (no geometry edits): cue_nosing=False (fully worn paint — realistic old dock) and cue_material_break=False (concrete apron), plus the hazard_stairs=False flat control, to decorrelate paint/material from the label.

Raise band wear locally: drop_ratio 0.10 -> ~0.35 on the MainS span only (the judged corridor), leaving BayBack/BayN at 0.10 — creates multi-metre bare-lip gaps consistent with traffic-side wear and forces geometric edge learning.

Scatter 10-15 small deck-tinted concrete spall chips (0.03-0.08 m) along the lip x in [-0.4, 0] (D2 debris-style, seeded): arris spalling is standard on ageing docks and yields a few-px silhouette cue at h0.3 where the band compresses to 1 px.
Add a mirrored capture corridor gy=+4.0 (grid_views baseline swap, camera-side only) so the U-bend appears frame-right in half the cuts, breaking the left-bend position prior.

Texture the far side: 1-2 dark tyre-scuff arcs (existing gk_stain material, flush) on the apron at x 9-12 m — outside every hiding limit at h0.9/h1.8 — so far-side depth is not a featureless grey field.

scenes.drop_type: construction floor opening (non-stair drop, 3.0 m)
scenes.drop_summary: Frame-stage slab (z=0, broom concrete) with an unguarded 1.5x2.0 m opening (west lip = x=0), basement at z=-3.0; charred formwork skirt under the lip guarantees a black frame, sun bounce lights the basement east wall to 'dark but not 0'. Designed as the strongest black-rectangle confusion pair with sceneN2 (fresh asphalt patch, GT negative). Context cues: 9 rebar stubs + debris ring + worn yellow U marking (2 lines y=+-1.05 + transverse x=-3.0). cue_nosing/railing=False — unguarded is the point. Registry: scenes/batch1/sceneD2_floor_opening.py SCENE_CONFIG + PARAMS[opening/skirt/lower/rebar/debris/gkit]; renders look_check/sceneD2/260816_w4_final33_on.

cues.notes: Opening rim vs interior: extreme at near range — h0.9_d2 centre-strip interior L=8.2 vs deck 180 (>20x). h1.8_d5 opening 259 px tall, interior mean L=122 vs deck 152; h1.8_d10 52 px; h0.9_d10 thin 26 px band. At h0.3 the rim collapses: d2 a 5-px black sliver (L=90), d5/d10 <=1-2 px (L=79/73) — the lip line is effectively gone at grazing.

Deliberately absent: the far side of the opening is the SAME broom slab (no material break across the walking axis), which is what lets the opening flatten into the floor at grazing. The only texture change is INTO the interior (formwork wall, charred skirt) — counted under far_side/shadow. cue_material_break toggles basement material only.

The black L-frame (charred skirt sRGB 0.042 + interior self-shadow) IS the black-rectangle signature: very-dark (L<40) fraction inside the opening bbox = 29.6% at h0.9_d2, 10.4% at h1.8_d5, 3.5% at h1.8_d2; falls to 0.3%/0.0% at h0.3_d5/d10 (8.2% at h0.3_d2 as a thin sliver). Sun az +5.5 deg keeps shadows nearly axial so the frame stays symmetric.

Through the opening the basement east wall is visible with a vertical gradient (sun pool bounce, designed 'dark but not fully 0'): lit-tan fraction inside the bbox 17-34% at h0.9/h1.8 d2-d5, interior mean L 84-130 vs deck 143-180. This is genuine interior depth (unlike D1 where no vertical face is ever seen). Fully occluded at h0.3 (all d); compressed to 26/52 px at h0.9_d10/h1.8_d10.

cue_nosing=False — no paint on the lip itself (nosing params dormant: 0.15 m yellow, proud 0.002). The nearest paint is the U marking inset 0.15 m (longitudinal) to 3.0 m (transverse) from the lip — classified under signage_or_marking.
Not applicable (construction site, documented out-of-scope in gkit comment, tactile=()).

The opening is unguarded (the scene's point; opening_rail params dormant). A 3-panel movable safety-fence row stands >=3.9 m NORTH as a single straight run that does not enclose the opening — visible upper-left in most presets, i.e. a guard element that co-occurs with the hazard without guarding it (see shortcut_risks).
Flush-cut lip, no upstand. Note the 0.05 m earth->slab step at the site boundary (the ribbed band crossing the foreground at h0.3_d10) is a visible NON-hazard edge — a useful built-in hard negative.
Only leaf/organic litter flecks on the outside earth (dirt_park texture); no vegetation line relates to the opening.
Dry site, no standing water in basement or on slab.

Yellow U opening-marking paint (opens toward the opening, transverse at x=-3.0): dominant at mid presets — 15.3% of lower-half pixels at h0.9_d5, 3.9% at h1.8_d5, still salient compressed at h0.3_d2/d5; near-invisible at h0.9_d10 (0.01%). DISCREPANCY vs spec: gkit prescribes '20-30% yellow remaining' wear, but the renders show a solid, saturated, continuous U — currently the single most saturated object in frame. Green placard bands on colonnade columns are textless context only.
Matte site (slab/earth/bags rough 0.88-0.95); rebar metallic 0.8 but 6 mm radius — no measurable glints at 512 spp noon.

The lip constellation breaks the horizon exactly at the hazard: 9 rebar stubs (h 0.36, 6 straight + 2 bent + 1 hooked, rust-brown) and a 46-piece debris ring (0.03-0.13 m, 60% within 0.55 m of the lip), plus the far-lip broom-ridge band. At h0.3 (all d) these are the ONLY visible evidence of the drop (direct rim <=2 px); at d10 the cluster shrinks to a few px. Caveat: debris renders with a bright white-speckled gravel texture (L~200), visually alien to the slab-grey debris_colors in PARAMS.

shortcut_risks: White gravel-textured chunks + rust-brown stub constellation == opening: these textures/objects appear only at the hazard, and at h0.3 they are the sole evidence — a pure context regressor works without ever seeing the drop.
Solid saturated yellow U == opening 3 m ahead (renders ignore the documented 20-30%-remaining wear, making the U far more reliable than intended).

Very dark rectangle == hole: the skirt guarantees near-zero luminance at close range (L=8 at h0.9_d2); must keep sceneN2 (dark asphalt patch, negative) co-batched or this collapses to a brightness threshold.

Static dressing memorization: fence row upper-left, white cement-bag pallet stack, twin tan gravel domes right, crane top-right sit in identical frame positions across all presets — scene-identity features that predict the label corpus-wide.
Footprint trail leading to the lip co-occurs with the opening (trail from (-7,-0.9) to (-1.2,-0.3)) — a subtle directional context cue.
suggestions: Re-tint roughly half the debris chunks to the slab-grey debris_colors already in PARAMS (0.18-0.30 band) instead of the bright white gravel texture — keeps the ring realistic (crushed cut-out concrete matches the slab it was cut from) while removing the white-beacon shortcut.

Apply D1-style seeded dropout to the U marking segments to actually hit the gkit '20-30% yellow remaining' prescription (currently rendered solid) — realism-prescribed and weakens the yellow-U shortcut simultaneously.

Add a few 0.02-0.05 m arris spalls/chamfer bites along the west lip (on the slab side, GT-V-safe: nothing overhangs the void) so the lip keeps a geometric micro-signature at h0.3 where the rim is otherwise <=2 px.

Batch-render dormant cue variants: opening_rail=True for a fraction of captures (guarded openings are the common real case) and nosing=True for another fraction, decorrelating 'bare unguarded lip' from the label; keep the hazard_stairs=False fill control paired.
Reseed debris (seed 2907) and jitter rebar stub positions per capture round within their current envelopes so the exact constellation cannot be memorized (counts and GT-V clearances kept).

Use the existing dome_rotation_step 15-deg sun sweep for +-15-30 deg azimuth variants: the interior lit-tan-over-black pattern then varies, so the fixed 'tan band inside dark frame' template does not become the opening's fingerprint.

scenes.drop_type: underground car-park entry ramp trench (3.96 m, 8.5%->17%->8.5% grades) + adjoining door-guarded stair shaft (3.96 m at x=11.20, off the judgment axis)
scenes.drop_summary: Drop edge x=0 where the estate carriageway meets the 6 m wide covered trench. At h0.3 the deck geometrically compresses (sight line 4.86 deg > atan(0.3/d) for d>=3.5) and the full-length canopy + 16 soffit lamp battens deliberately equalize interior brightness (deck L 147+-44 vs sidewalk 143+-10 at h0.9_d2), so the ground-plane read vanishes by design; the mouth line, trench walls and the surrounding structure carry the evidence instead. Judgment presets run the vehicle centreline y=0; the stair-head drop is guarded by an entrance door and appears only in entry_approach/stair_head cuts.

cues.notes: Mouth line = trench-grate/coping band, L 109+-28 vs sidewalk 151+-15 at h0.9_d5 (28% step). At h0.3_d10 it thins to a ~14-row slot, L 92 vs 138 surroundings — still present but marginal.

Across the mouth the cue is suppressed BY DESIGN: lamplit deck L 147+-44 vs sidewalk 143+-10 (Δ<3%) — GT-58 declared photometric equalization. The near-side transverse rhythm (interlocking aggregate -> grey crossing slab -> dark grate/coping) is the real texture signal; deck grooving starts only at x=3.6 and is invisible at h0.3.

Canopy + soffit battens intentionally remove the dark-trench leg of the illusion (baseline wall-shadow band measured mean 11 before lamps). Residual: thin shadow slot under the far coping and the mouth beam line.

Far trench headwall + basement portal visible at every preset incl. h0.3_d10; portal opening L 19+-41 vs headwall 61+-7 (3.1x darker). Cheek walls with chevrons read from d2/d5 — the trench interior is never fully hidden.
cue_nosing False (weak custom on basement stairs); the pedestrian stair is inside the shaft, off all preset frames.
cue_tactile False by v5.2 user ruling (rare in reality); bollard-front and stair-head tactile paths kept only as ablation arms — not in final33_on renders.

Continuous white-framed glass balustrade screens on both copings for the whole trench (08-05 doctrine: guard itself is the cue), canopy columns on the coping, height bar over the mouth. Visible in all 9 presets. The mouth itself is open (vehicle path) — correct practice.

Flush coping at the rim is the scene's deliberate below-code identity (no G13 parapet). Present instead: ramp cheek kerbs h0.12/w0.30 with yellow/black blocks (statutory §6(1)5(c)), footway kerb 0.150 (GT-5) with crossing turn-downs. At h0.3_d10 kerb blocks shrink to small yellow marks.
Trees/hedges are estate dressing seen through the glass screens — context only, nothing grows at the trench edge.
None.

Yellow centre line begins exactly at x=0 (approach carries white dashes — a marking discontinuity at the edge); yellow/black chevron bands + reflective strips on trench walls (patch RGB ~(138,132,58)); y/b height-limit bar (prominent at h1.8); parapet entry sign; 안내/INFORMATION board. At h0.3_d10 reduced to chevron slivers + the dash rhythm breaking into the trench.
Sidewalk sheen pools before the mouth vs matte lamplit deck; glass reflections. Marginal and lighting-dependent — not a reliable edge cue.
The full-length canopy + glass corridor + portal headwall form a building-scale frame around the drop, dominant in every preset — strongest single evidence family, and also the main shortcut vector.

shortcut_risks: Structure-context shortcut: 'canopy + glass corridor = drop' — the detector can key on the building-scale frame and never learn the ground-plane evidence; an uncovered trench elsewhere would be missed and any covered walkway could false-positive.
Signage co-occurrence: yellow/black chevrons, height bar and the white->yellow centre-line switch all begin exactly at x=0 — 'yellow marking = drop'.
Dark-hole shortcut: the basement portal (L~19) is the darkest region in every frame and always co-locates with the drop — 'dark region = drop'.
The deliberate brightness equalization (deck==sidewalk) means the model that DOES learn ground evidence here learns 'no contrast + structure = drop', which anti-transfers to open trenches.
suggestions: Per-batten lumen jitter / 2-3 dark battens among the 16 soffit lamps (부분 소등 is normal practice) — decorrelates the uniformly-lit interior signature without touching geometry.
Twin tire-wear bands + faint oil staining on the first metres of the deck (universal on real entry ramps) — restores a deck-texture cue readable at h0.9 with no new signs.
Paint-wear/fade variation on the yellow centre line and chevrons so the signage cue is graded, not binary-saturated.
Rust/water streaks under the trench-grate lip to widen the mouth slot's tonal signature at grazing h0.3 angles (plain weathering, realism-preserving).
Data-side: render the existing cue_railing / cue_scene_dressing ablation arms so the structure-context shortcut is measurable against ground-only evidence.

scenes.drop_type: Potemkin illusory monumental stair — 6.0 m drop over 40 steps (riser 0.150, tread 0.340), 3 landings, width taper y±3 -> y±5
scenes.drop_summary: Drop edge x=0 at the marble terrace -> concrete flight boundary. The illusion is the frozen research identity: from the approach only landings are visible and the flight self-occludes, so the terrace reads as continuous with the lower plaza. Measured: at h0.3 all three distances show NO dark region at the edge at all (frame p5 luminance 134-149); the compressed flight band at h0.9_d5 is L 188+-11 vs terrace 200+-9 (Δ6%). Evidence lives almost entirely in the far side (buildings with occluded ground floors, shrub crowns cut by the terrace horizon) and the raking parapet wedges at the frame edges.

cues.notes: No shadow, no upstand at x=0. The seam is a faint tone boundary: strongest measured step at the edge zone is the vegetation/building band (row grad -72), not the ground line. At h1.8_d2 the first nosing lines resolve; at h0.3 the flight subtends <10 rows.

cue_material_break True (marble terrace vs concrete flight, GT-70) — but measured Δ is only ~7%: flight 184+-14 vs terrace 199+-8 at h1.8_d2. Coursing joints (7 mm, band_dark) add texture at h1.8. Entirely self-occluded at h0.3. Also real: transverse trench drain at x=-2.59 + gullies at x=-0.95 give faint pre-edge lines (grad -22 at h0.9_d5).
Noon sun leaves no cast shadow at the nosing lines from the approach side — the brightness leg of the illusion. Only small parapet shadows on the flight, visible from h1.8.

The load-bearing cue: backdrop blocks with ground floors occluded, planter/shrub crowns cut by the terrace horizon, lamp-pole bases hidden, fountain + bollard row visible only from h1.8. At h0.3 it demands inference (missing building bases) rather than direct sight of a lower surface.
cue_nosing False.
Identity conflict — §12.4 hidden-illusion group; gate B12 _inv_hidden_illusion enforces OFF. Do not add.

No rail (GT-78 withdrew the wall-top handrail). The raking side parapets (top 0.950 m over the nosing line, width 0.5) act as flank guards and read as descending wedges at the frame edges; nothing guards the head of the flight — by identity. At h0.3 the wedges shrink to corner slivers.
Terrace runs flush into the first riser — the illusion requires it. (A parapet kerb exists in the dressing away from the edge.)

Shrub/tree crowns of the LOWER plaza poke above the terrace horizon with bases hidden — a real depth cue at h0.3_d2/d5. Autumn leaf litter on the terrace is a distractor, not edge evidence (authoring kept it out of the h0.3 band).
Fountain hint is dry geometry, far side, h1.8-only.
One plaza info sign exists (cue_sign True) but sits off the judgment axis — visible in no preset frame; zero marking at the edge.
Matte stone throughout; building window glass only.

Raking/stepped parapet shoulders (zigzag profile clear at h1.8_d5) and the truncated vertical extent of the backdrop blocks. The single most reliable geometric giveaway above h0.9; nearly gone in a centre crop at h0.3.

shortcut_risks: At h0.3 the drop is carried by ONE family — far-side occlusion (building bases + shrub crowns). Fog, tighter crop or backdrop changes make the drop invisible; a model trained here may learn 'white civic backdrop + cream plaza = drop at fixed image band', which is scene-id memorization, not detection.
Near-edge ground fixture regularity: trench drain at x=-2.59 here, manhole at x=-2.60 in scene15 — a cross-scene 'dark transverse fixture ~2.5 m before edge' correlation a model can exploit.
The illusion's negative-space signature (zero texture change + zero shadow + level skyline) is itself learnable as 'scene14 = drop', which anti-transfers.
Leaf litter clusters appear on the terrace in most presets — seasonal dressing co-occurring with the drop.
suggestions: Widen the measured material break within realism: the concrete flight is only Δ~7% from the marble terrace — a darker broom-finish tint or stronger coursing joint tone (parameter-level, GT-70 family) would make the h0.9/h1.8 boundary measurable without touching the h0.3 illusion (still self-occluded there).
Rain-wash weathering streak along the first nosing line (water sheets over a stair head in reality) — a thin tone line at x=0 readable at h0.9, invisible at h0.3 grazing, preserving the identity.
De-template the backdrop: vary plinth/ground-floor opening heights across the five blocks so base-occlusion inference generalizes instead of matching one facade pattern.
Keep tactile/nosing OFF (gate B12 identity) — strengthen nothing at the edge itself beyond weathering.
Data-side: pair every batch with the hazard_stairs=False flat arm (existing toggle) as the same-framing hard negative, directly attacking the scene-id shortcut.

scenes.drop_type: walled hillside alley stair — 4.25 m total (12 steps + 1.5 m landing + 13 steps behind a 25 deg bend), corridor 1.2 m wide
scenes.drop_summary: Drop edge x=0 where the upper alley floor (effective albedo 0.30 after GT-121) ends between flanking house walls. Treads are self-occluded on approach; evidence is the crisp floor-end line against the shadowed lower alley (floor L 193+-17 vs beyond 74+-68 at h0.9_d2; edge gradient +129/row at h0.3_d2) and the lower village visible below eye level (pastel upper storeys, green urethane rooftops, landing planter). The 2.21 m behind the 25 deg bend carries no cue at all — declared research identity. Guard = the walls themselves (cue_railing False, survey-based).

cues.notes: h0.3_d2: floor 187 vs beyond 68 (Δ~119 L, max grad +129/row). h0.9_d2: 193 vs 74. Degrades with distance: h0.9_d10 grad -11/row (still a clean line), h0.3_d10 grad ~-5/row, Δ<10 L — near-invisible at the grazing far preset.

cue_material_break True (stair 0.20 neutral vs floor 0.30) but treads are self-occluded from the whole approach row; beyond the edge one sees facades, not ground. Construction joints deliberately EXCLUDED at x=0 (edge exclusion) — no artificial line marks the edge.

Ambiguous double role: raking wall shadows cross the floor obliquely as distractors (±40 L bands), while much of the beyond-edge darkness at h0.9 is shade of the lower corridor — the edge step is partly shadow-driven, not geometry-driven. GT-121 raised albedos so shaded surfaces hold >=0.2.

The dominant family: lower houses' upper storeys and green rooftops BELOW eye level in every preset (even h0.3_d10 shows facade bases cut by the edge); landing planter + shrub visible below from h0.9_d2/h1.8. Unambiguous 'ground continues lower' evidence.
Painted nosing is not alley practice — key reserved, OFF.
Not the practice (sample p~0.05) — forbidden by the ground profile.

cue_railing False by survey (0/12 code guardrails on photographed hillside alley stairs); walls carry the guard (§15(1)2). ON arm = one wall-bracketed φ34 pipe over the upper flight only; lower flight bare either way. Not in final33_on.
Floor runs flush into the first riser; no upstand. Flanking 석축/walls are corridor sides, not edge protection.
Weed tufts on the upper floor (auto-clamped AWAY from the edge by the GT-E5 ramp), hedge crowns atop the flank walls, landing planter below the edge. Depth-supporting but sparse.
None (U-gutter is covered).
cue_sign False — not implemented; zero markings (correct for the setting).
Matte concrete/plaster throughout; no gloss transition at the edge.

Corridor perspective collapse: flank wall top lines and house eaves step down past x=0, converging walls frame the void, roofs sit below the horizon. Reads at every preset; at h1.8 the stepped descent of the wall tops is explicit.

shortcut_risks: 'Bright floor -> dark region ahead = drop': the beyond-edge contrast is substantially shadow-driven; without shadow-band negatives (sceneN1) in the same mix, a shade line becomes a false drop trigger — and a sun-lit lower alley would weaken the true one.
Near-edge fixture regularity: manhole at x=-2.60 (network-derived) mirrors scene14's trench at -2.59 — 'dark disc/line ~2.5 m before edge' cross-scene correlation.
'Green urethane roof or pastel facade in mid-frame = drop below': in this corpus those appear below eye level only across drops.
Corridor-context shortcut: a 1.2 m double-walled alley ALWAYS descends here — no flat twin with the same walls exists in the judged set, so 'narrow walled corridor = stair drop' is free to learn.

Everything the model can use is one family (lower-village visibility + its shadowed void): fog/night or a blank retaining wall beyond would blind it, especially at h0.3_d10 where the edge gradient is already ~5 L/row.
suggestions: Render the hazard_stairs=False flat-alley arm (existing toggle) as the same-context hard negative — the single most direct attack on the corridor shortcut.
Mix in the cue_railing ON arm (wall-bracketed φ34 pipe, survey-vetted realistic) for part of the data so bare-edge is not a constant of the scene.

Worn-arris tone on the first 2-3 nosings (polished/chipped old concrete, not paint — distinct from the reserved cue_nosing) to give a minimal h0.9_d2/h1.8 edge confirmation; walked-surface tone, so propose for user verdict first.
Sun-azimuth jitter across data renders to decorrelate the shadow-driven component of the edge contrast from the geometric one.
Leave the 25 deg bend concealment and the h0.3_d10 weakness untouched — declared research identity of the scene.

scenes.drop_type: non-stair longitudinal drop: unguarded roadside concrete drainage channel (trapezoid, top 1.0 m / bottom 0.5 m / depth 0.8 m) running parallel to the travel axis (+X); walkable cover slab ends at x=0, open channel x 0..38 m, GT = 0.8 m drop over the opening band y ±0.5
scenes.drop_summary: Camera line rides the channel centerline (gy=0) on the cover slab. The drop announces itself almost entirely as a dark interior band: cover slab linear L≈0.22 vs opening interior L≈0.003–0.008 (Weber ≈ −0.97). Apparent dark-slit height at image centre: 230 px (h0.3_d2) → 84 px (h0.3_d5) → 36 px (h0.3_d10); at h0.3_d10 the far half (x≳20 m) merges completely with the far lip/verge — the designed grazing concealment. Road-side lip is flush (+2 mm) by design, no rail/curb/tactile (unguarded identity); the straw grass-overhang both marks and conceals the verge edge. 54–55% of opening-band pixels are L<0.06 in every preset.

cues.notes: Transverse cover-end edge at x=0 and longitudinal lip edges give near-total contrast: cover L≈0.22 (sRGB ~140,124,103) vs opening L≈0.003–0.008 (Weber ≈ −0.97); dark slit at col 960 = 230/84/36 px for h0.3 d2/d5/d10 and 116/231 px for h0.9/h1.8 at d10. At h0.3_d10 the opening line vanishes beyond x≈20 m (slit run ends 3 rows short of the x=38 projection); near field stays high-contrast.

Ordered sequence from road: asphalt (154,154,157; L 0.33) → white edge line (225; L 0.64–0.75) → concrete lip (L 0.19–0.21) → void; from verge: grass (147,145,88) → straw overhang (152,140,86) → weathered channel wall (wall_tint 0.55). Ribbed broom-finish cover slab is a distinctive approach texture. At h0.3 grazing the lip/overhang bands compress to <10 px and the sequence collapses to two tones.

Designed 55° oblique sun (SUN_AZ_OFFSET 201.5, elev 49.8°): road-side inner wall fully shaded, bed shadow boundary at y≈+0.054 → partial-shade interior (lit far wall/bed L 0.14–0.24 vs shaded 0.003–0.01), not a black card. Reads as a distinct boundary line at h0.9_d2, h1.8_d2/d5 and channel_reveal; at h0.3 it merges into the single dark slit. Fixed sun azimuth bakes one shadow signature into every render.

Sunlit verge-side inner wall, bed slab and leaf-litter lenses (6 carpet lobes + 160 scattered leaves) read clearly at h0.9_d2/d5 and all h1.8 presets, proving 'below-grade content'. At h0.3 only the first ~3 m of interior shows anything but black; at h0.9_d10 the interior narrows to a 116 px band with litter barely resolvable.
Stairs-only key, unused by design (cue_nosing reserved).
cue_tactile=False — not customary on a rural roadside channel (ground_kit P17 verge_rural enforces zero urban infrastructure); code path exists for a counterfactual twin.
cue_railing=False is the scene identity ('being unguarded is the identity'); a single pipe-rail line on the verge side is implemented and can be toggled on for a guarded twin.
Deliberate absence: road-side lip flush with the roadway (top +2 mm only), docstring states 'no level-difference cue'. Verified in oblique_cross — no step shadow at the lip.

Continuous low straw overhang strips (12 segments, h 5–8 cm, ≤5 cm projection over the opening) along y=+0.5 plus ground-kit edge weeds. Dual-role cue: marks the channel line from the road/high views but CONCEALS the edge from the verge-side approach (verge_walk). Chroma barely differs from the verge (152,140,86 vs 147,145,88; R/G 1.09 vs 1.02) so it reads via lump geometry/shadow, not colour; at h0.3_d10 it is a few pixels.
Dry channel by spec (dry concrete + leaf litter); no water pixels.

No hazard signage (cue_sign off). Indirect only: white road edge line at y=−0.95 (L 0.64–0.75 vs road 0.33) runs the whole scene 0.45 m parallel to the lip, plus centre dashes. Usable by a detector as 'drop just beyond the white line' — a within-scene shortcut, not a legitimate drop marking.
All edge materials rough (asphalt 0.85, concrete ~0.6–0.9, leaves 0.9); no water film, no metal at the edge. No specular signature distinguishes the drop.

Trapezoid mouth (1.0/0.5/0.8) legible at d2 presets and channel_reveal; box-culvert headwall + dark recess (constant 0.030, L≈0.13 displayed) anchors the far end of the channel line at x=38; opening taper toward the vanishing point. From the road side (oblique_cross, depression ~18°) the near lip occludes all but the top ~0.3 m of the far wall; at h0.3_d10 the silhouette reduces to a 1D line.

shortcut_risks: 'Elongated near-black band parallel to the travel axis = drop': 54–55% of opening-band pixels are L<0.06 in all 9 presets; a plain luminance-threshold detector solves this scene. sceneN1 (shadow band) / sceneN2 (asphalt patch) are the intended negatives — they must stay co-batched at meaningful ratios.
'Straw hedge lip beside a dark line = drop edge': the overhang co-occurs 1:1 with the opening; grass_overhang=False twin exists but only as a look-check toggle.
'White edge line + light concrete lip band = drop 0.45 m to its left': the road marking parallels the full length of the hazard.
'Ribbed broom-finish slab underfoot = drop ahead': the cover-slab texture appears only on the hazard approach in this scene.
Positional prior: all grid presets ride gy=0 (channel centerline) so the drop is always a centred vertical band; fixed SUN_AZ_OFFSET=201.5 bakes a single interior-shade signature.
suggestions: Sweep the existing dome/sun azimuth knob (±30–60° around 201.5) across data renders so the interior partial-shade boundary (y≈+0.054) moves and sometimes reverses wall roles — removes the fixed shadow signature without touching geometry.
Add off-centerline camera lines to the render set (e.g. gy=−0.9 lip line and gy=+1.2 verge line alongside gy=0) — camera-only change that breaks the centred-band positional prior.

Feed the already-built toggle twins into the training mix (grass_overhang=False exposed-edge, cue_material_break=False asphalt-lip, minority cue_railing=True) so no single co-occurrence (straw band, lip band, unguardedness) is a necessary condition of the drop.

Small realistic aging on the drop edge: a few 1–2 cm spall notches/broken corners on the cover-slab end (x=0) and lip arris — aged roadside concrete — gives the edge a silhouette cue that survives overcast/rotated light; GT band unchanged.

A dried flow-stain/silt tongue along the invert centre (standard in real drainage channels) so the interior reads by texture as well as shadow when the sun rotates — strengthens far_side_visible_depth without new assets.

scenes.drop_type: non-stair indoor drop: subway platform edge → track trough, 1.15 m (walk z=0 → ballast −1.15), edge lines at y=±2.0 with no guard; fully sealed interior lit only by 30 ceiling emissive panels above the platforms (none above the track)
scenes.drop_summary: At grazing (h0.3) the trough floor is geometrically occluded at ALL distances (eye 0.3 m, edge 1.6 m left: the sight ray over the edge would first touch the floor at y=+5.7, beyond the far edge), so the platform reads as one continuous floor — the designed hazard. Surviving evidence at h0.3 is symbolic, not geometric: the amber tactile double band (rgb ~45,28,2; B≈0; only 1.2–1.7× walk luminance — chroma-carried) and the yellow nosing line (L 0.03–0.05 near, decaying to 0.006 below walk level by x≥12 m). The trough is near-black everywhere (row-set frac(L<0.02) 0.79–0.96; sleepers L 0.0004–0.003), contradicting the scene's own checklist target that sleepers/railheads should be 'barely readable, not full black'. Displayed step at h0.3_d5: walk rgb(40,32,22) vs trough band rgb(12,9,3).

cues.notes: Walk L 0.016 (rgb 40,32,22) vs visible trough band L 0.004 (rgb 12,9,3) at h0.3_d5 — ratio ≈3.7 but only ~28 sRGB counts absolute (whole floor lives below L 0.03); at h0.9_d5 band L 0.0023 → ratio ≈8. The luminance boundary alone is marginal at grazing; the geometric edge line is effectively drawn by the nosing chroma. At h0.3_d10 the band thins further and far-x nosing decays below walk luminance.

Unmistakable ordered band sequence at every preset: broom-finish walk → amber tactile ×2 (0.3 m each) → yellow nosing → black void → far coping/fascia → far platform + benches. Band widths compress with distance: tactile 343→30 px, nosing 66→6 px from x=1 to x=25 across presets; at h0.3_d10 the sequence is a few pixels but its order is still unique to the edge.

No sun and no window (sealed shell, dome contribution 0): there is no cast shadow line. The trough darkness is an illumination-falloff gradient (panels only above platforms, direct-illuminance ratio ≈0.26 × albedo factor ~7), which functions as region darkness, not a line cue.

Sleepers measure L 0.0004–0.003 (rgb 2–11) at every preset = unreadable black; ballast likewise (trough frac(L<0.02) 0.79–0.96). Railheads read only as near-field specular glints (see specular_change). At h0.3 the trough floor is geometrically occluded by the near edge at all distances (depression 10.6° < required), so depth content is invisible in principle, not just dark. Violates the scene's own checklist item 4 ('barely readable, not full black').

0.12 m yellow edge line (0.85,0.72,0.10), proud 2 mm: near-field L 0.03–0.05 = 3–5× walk at all heights; clearly traceable to the vanishing point at h0.9/h1.8. Under h0.3 it decays to L 0.006–0.007 (below walk 0.010) by x≥12 m and its screen width is 6–9 px at x=25 — still present as a chroma line but no longer bright.

Two 0.30 m rows, 0.3 m back from the edge, with real dot relief (PointInstancer, r17×h5 mm — dots resolve individually at d2 and edge_graze, giving silhouette texture at grazing). Colour is dark amber rgb ~(45,28,2): R/G≈1.6 with B≈0 — a pure chroma cue; luminance only 1.2–1.7× walk (L 0.011–0.018), so on a monochrome/luma basis the band nearly disappears. Band width 343→30 px across x/presets.

Barrier railing only at the platform END (x=45.4, tunnel side) — a distant grey silhouette against the portal in the d-presets and edge_graze; the drop edge itself is deliberately unguarded (hazard identity). At h0.3 it is a few dim pixels at the vanishing point.
Edge is flush; the 'bright 6 cm coping' lives on the vertical fascia face and renders near-black in edge_approach (fascia band rgb ≲12) — it currently contributes no visible step or bright rim.
Fully indoor scene — no vegetation.
Dry interior; no water pixels.

No drop-directed signage (cue_sign off). Wall signage exists as context only (textless nameplates, 2 dim lightboxes, orange line band, 4 ceiling hangers at |y|=2.6 — the hangers do sit directly above the warning band, a mild indirect correlate). The yellow edge line is counted under nosing_strip.

Polished railheads (metallic 0.85, rough 0.14) glint near-field: railhead L up to 0.079 at h1.8_d10 x=1 (rgb ~80 neutral) ≈20× the trough, visible at h0.9/h1.8 for x≲6–12 m, then dies (L 0.001–0.002 beyond). Fully occluded at h0.3 (trough interior hidden). The only specular event in the scene, and it lies inside the drop — a genuine but range-limited depth cue.

Three-layer composition (near platform / black trough band / far platform with benches, doors, skirting, second yellow pair) orders depth at h0.9/h1.8 and in track_reveal; the black portal at x=46 terminates the band. At h0.3 the layering flattens into horizontal stripes and the far platform floor (L 0.012–0.020) nearly matches the near walk (0.010–0.016) — the 'one continuous floor' illusion measured, not just asserted.

shortcut_risks: 'Amber/yellow strip with B-channel ≈ 0 = drop': tactile+nosing co-occur 1:1 with the edge and there is not a single yellow-without-drop pixel in the scene; the tactile source texture itself has B≈0.0006 (GT-116 note) — a trivially learnable spectral signature.

'Darkest horizontal band = drop': trough frac(L<0.02) is 0.79–0.96; the only comparable black (tunnel portal) is also above track — the scene contains no dark-but-safe counterexample on the floor plane.
Indoor-context prior: this is the library's only fully indoor scene, so 'emissive ceiling panels + tile walls ⇒ platform drop present' is a scene-level shortcut no pixel evidence can break.
Positional prior: the drop is always exactly 1.6 m left of the camera line (gy=−3.6, edge y=−2.0), i.e. a left-of-frame band in all 9 presets; the mirrored near-platform view is never rendered.
Global exposure prior: the whole frame lives at L≈0.01 (an order dimmer than every outdoor scene) — a mean-luminance feature alone identifies D4 and hence 'drop'.
suggestions: Execute the scene's own checklist target: raise ballast/sleeper effective albedo within the GT-116 measured aging bands (ballast ~0.13 → 0.18–0.20, sleeper ~0.10 → 0.13) so sleepers/railheads become 'barely readable' at h0.9 instead of pure black — converts the drop from a flat black band into visible depth; zero geometry change.

Add the standard longitudinal guidance tactile strip (선형 유도블록) mid-platform (e.g. y≈−5, flat textless band, ubiquitous in Korean stations): creates realistic yellow-without-drop pixels inside the scene and breaks the 'yellow ⇒ edge' equivalence with no new sign.
Render the mirrored viewpoint from the far platform (gy=+3.6; geometry is already symmetric) and vary gy (−4.5/−3.0) — camera-only, removes the fixed left-offset positional prior.

Include cue_tactile=False / cue_nosing=False / cue_material_break=False toggle twins in the data mix so no single marking is a necessary condition of the drop (all three toggles already exist with invariant hazard geometry).

Lighten the fascia coping tint toward real light-concrete coping (the top 6 cm band already modelled but rendering near-black): yields a thin bright rim over the black trough on the far edge at h0.9+, adding a second geometric edge cue at zero layout cost.

scenes.drop_type: wide low-rise plaza stair (4 steps x 0.15 m riser, total 0.60 m; travel +X, top edge x=0, stair width 11 m)
scenes.drop_summary: Designed stealth hazard: upper and lower plazas are the same granite family, so from grazing viewpoints the two surfaces meet in a single image row with no visible depth gap. Judged presets (eye y=-2.75, pitch 10 deg down) show the drop mainly as a paving-module boundary line plus stainless stair railings when they enter the frame. Charcoal decoration bands (2.7 m pitch, parallel to the edge) are 2-3x higher-contrast than the true edge in every d10 frame.

cues.notes: The projected top-nosing line is a clean luminance step where the coarse upper slabs end: measured (row-mean, central 550 px strip) 180->206 (dL +26) at h0.3_d2 (row 498), +29 at h0.9_d5, +25 at h0.9_d2, +23 at h1.8_d5, +22 at h1.8_d10 (Weber ~11-15%). It is a material line, not a depth line. At h0.3_d10 the far side compresses to <10 rows crowded by benches/planters and the strongest local gradients are the charcoal bands (dL 60-75), not the edge; at h1.8_d2 the edge projects below the frame bottom (predicted row ~1519 of 1080).

Module + tint change: upper plaza plaza_light 1.80 m/tile coarse white slabs vs lower plaza plaza_lower 0.70 m/tile fine pavers with warm tint (1.06,1.0,0.94). Measured far-side R/B 1.11 at h0.9_d2 vs 1.01 near side; at grazing h0.3_d2 the tint washes out to R/B 1.03 and only the joint-frequency change remains. cue_material_break=False is a wired ablation arm that removes this cue entirely.

Noon front light (sun az ~205 deg, elev 49.8) shades the riser faces, but risers are invisible from the upper approach, so no shadow band marks the edge in any of the 9 presets. Incidental decoys: long lamp/railing shadows cross the foreground in d10 frames; railing shadow zig-zags on the treads only in the non-judged edge_closeup cut.

At h0.9/h1.8 the lower plaza reads as a lower terrace via furniture (benches, planter walls whose caps sit near upper-floor level) and the retaining wall + lawn behind. At all h0.3 presets the two pavements appear exactly coplanar - the 0.6 m offset and the ~2.5-4 m of hidden ground are unreadable (the scene's intended stealth).
Treads and nosings are the same white granite; no anti-slip or contrast strip (edge_closeup confirms bare arris). Leaves drifted along the top joint at h0.9_d2 form an accidental faint marker line.
cue_tactile=False by v5.2 realism ruling (rare in reality); statutory-band code path kept for ablation only.

Stainless guard+handrail assemblies at both stair flanks (y=+-5.5) and a centre rail; crisp against brick/lawn at every d5/d10 preset, and the top-rail slope descending past the edge is itself a geometric drop hint. All three d2 presets crop them out (camera y=-2.75 sits between centre and south rail), leaving d2 frames rail-free.
Drop edge is flush (no upstand). A 150 mm granite lawn kerb exists up-slope at the lawn strip - a registered separate drop row (lawn_kerb_N/S) and a potential confuser, not an edge cue here.
No planting bound to the edge. Lawn strip, elm rows and planters C/E (lower plaza) are context dressing beyond the far side.
Still basin sits far out in the lawn (visible mid-frame at h0.9_d2/h1.8_d2/h1.8_d5); unrelated to the drop.

cue_sign=True builds one Korean facility sign, but it appears in none of the 9 judged presets. Meanwhile the charcoal granite bands read as edge-parallel ground 'markings' (L 116-135 vs slab 190-206) - a marking-like signal that is NOT the edge.
Matte granite on both sides of the edge (rough ~0.9); no specular differential across the line. Only rails (metallic 0.9) and the distant basin are specular.
Interior edge - no skyline break. Weak hints: descending handrail silhouettes (d5/d10), furniture cut at lower-terrace heights, leaf line at the nosing (h0.9_d2).

shortcut_risks: Charcoal transverse bands (2.7 m pitch, parallel to the edge) appear between camera and edge in every d10 frame with dL 60-75 - 2-3x the true edge step (22-30); a model can learn 'dark band = edge' or use band count as range-to-edge.

'Fine pavement above coarse pavement = drop': the module-frequency step is the dominant cue and this scene offers no counterexample of the same module change without a drop (cue_material_break ablation exists but is off in data unless rendered).
Warm far-side tint (R/B ~1.11 at h0.9_d2) = drop side.
Stainless railings never occur without the stair - railing presence alone predicts the drop.
Leaf drift concentrates along the nosing joint (h0.9_d2) - leaf line = edge.
Fixed composition prior: edge always a horizontal line at a camera-height-predictable row; sun azimuth fixed at ~205 deg.
suggestions: Add a sun-azimuth variation arm (SUN_AZ_OFFSET override, e.g. +-60-90 deg) so an oblique riser shadow occasionally draws a thin dark line at the top nosing - the only realistic edge-bound cue that would survive h0.3_d10 grazing without new objects.

Author a subtle worn/soiled nosing line along the top arris using the existing stain-decal language (plaza tint one step down, e.g. 0.62 band a few cm wide) - real granite stair heads carry this; it gives the edge its own signature independent of the module change.
Decouple the band shortcut: repeat one charcoal band on the lower plaza (plausible design continuity) and randomize band phase between renders so band-to-edge distance is not a constant.
Break 'fine = lower' purity: lay a fine-module border course on the upper plaza along the lawn kerb (common plaza detailing) so the module change also occurs without a drop.
Render some data arms with cue_material_break=False (already wired) and with small camera-y jitter so railings sometimes enter d2 frames and the model cannot rely on one cue per pose.
Randomize leaf drift so leaf lines also form along bands and planter feet, not only at the nosing.

scenes.drop_type: underpass pit mouth: 20-step stair, 3.38 m drop at x=0 behind a +0.18 m flood-sill up-step; fully guarded (perimeter rail, canopy, sill handrails)
scenes.drop_summary: A descending pit cut into the sidewalk, announced almost entirely by erected structure: 3-sided perimeter guard on the parapet, full-length canopy on 5 column pairs, limestone flood-sill apron (+0.18 m), tile-clad pit walls under granite coping, and a dark self-shadowed mouth. From h0.3 the pit floor/steps are invisible and at d5/d10 even the mouth is hidden behind the sill riser - all surviving evidence is above-ground furniture. Measured: mouth band L=42 vs apron 189 at h0.3_d2 (4.5:1); pit interior L=65 vs 195 at h1.8_d5 (3:1).

cues.notes: The true edge (apron top far rim at x=0) is nearly edge-on from h0.3 (eye 0.30 vs apron 0.18): no line of its own. What reads instead is the dark mouth beyond it: L 41.6+-2.5 vs lit apron 188.6 at h0.3_d2. At h0.3_d5/d10 the mouth is hidden behind the sill riser and the whole hazard region flattens to L 173 vs sidewalk 185 (dL 12, near-invisible on the ground plane).

Warm limestone apron (RGB 204/193/171, R/B 1.19) against neutral grey sidewalk blocks (195/195/193) flags the hazard zone starting 1.2 m before the edge; beyond the edge the far surface is the pit's shaded concrete/tile far wall (L 85+-30) - a vertical wall where a floor should be, a strong discontinuity signal at d2/d5.

The pit is self-shadowed (interior L 65-85 vs 190+ surround) so the mouth reads as a dark slot - effectively the edge line at d2. Canopy soffit/column shadows also band the apron (h0.9_d2) - decoy edges parallel to the true one.

Pit walls converge to the far retaining wall + coping; the interior (walls, floor patch L~106, tunnel mouth) is visible at d2 for all heights and partially at h0.9_d5/h1.8_d5/d10; descending in-pit handrails and the exit sign anchor below-grade reading at h0.9_d2/h1.8_d2/h1.8_d5. Fully hidden behind the sill apron at h0.3_d5/d10.

cue_nosing=True builds a yellow anti-slip strip on every one of the 20 steps (subway practice), but treads face away/below from the approach: the strips are visible in zero of the 9 judged presets (only in reverse/interior cuts such as inside_looking_up). As data, this cue exists only for viewpoints the presets never take.
cue_tactile=False (v5.2 ruling); ablation path kept.

Visible in ALL 9 presets: 3-sided perimeter guard (h 0.9 on the +0.18 parapet), sill flank handrails on RF-1 bolted base plates, plus 5 canopy column pairs reading as a fence-like colonnade. At h0.3_d10 this plus the apron band is essentially the entire hazard signal.

The +0.18 m flood-sill apron is a statutory up-step lip across the mouth; its bright limestone riser face bands every h0.3/h0.9 approach frame. Caution: it is labelled up_step in GT, and it visually pre-empts the true drop line 1.2 m behind it (mislocalization pull). Road curb (150 mm exposure) exists at frame edges, unrelated.
Only dressing: hedge blob at the far right corner, grass tufts in sidewalk joints. Nothing bound to the edge.
None.

Blue Korean exit sign (출구) inside the pit - visible at h0.9_d2, h1.8_d2, h1.8_d5; a blue ground-level noticeboard enters d10 frames (left, unrelated position). No warning marking on the walking surface itself.
