Stainless rails and canopy side glazing glint against matte block paving; the pit interior is matte-dark. No specular event on the ground plane at the edge itself.
Canopy roof + column pairs + railing lattice form an unmistakable subway-mouth structure silhouette in every preset - the scene's grazing-angle identity cue by design.

shortcut_risks: Guard-furniture co-occurrence: railing+canopy perfectly predict the drop here, yet a fully guarded pit is the least dangerous configuration - a model keyed to furniture will miss unguarded drops (scene03) and false-fire on guarded-but-flat structures (bus shelters, colonnades).

Darkness shortcut: 'dark slot between beige walls = drop' (mouth L 42-85 vs ~190 surround); fails under overcast/night and false-fires on shadow bands - keep sceneN1 (shadow_band decoy) paired in training mixes.
Limestone-color proxy: the warm apron band marks the hazard 1.2 m early; the model may localize the drop at the sill riser (an up-step, labelled up_step in GT) instead of x=0.
Blue sign = underpass co-occurrence.
Composition prior: pit always centered (gy=0), symmetric railing frame, edge horizontal.
suggestions: Give the ground plane one edge-bound cue that survives h0.3_d5/d10: a weathered/drip-stained darker top on the granite coping course along the apron's far rim (realistic coping stain), drawing a thin dark line exactly at x=0 above the sill riser.

Wet-day arm: a shallow puddle sheen on the lower landing visible through the mouth at d2 (plausible for an underpass) - adds a specular below-grade cue and weakens the 'void = uniformly dark' invariant.
Lighting diversity: an overcast-HDRI arm where the soffit-lit interior brightens (battens already modelled), so interior darkness is not the constant the model latches onto.
Decorrelate the canopy shadow: vary dome rotation between renders so the soffit shadow band on the apron does not always parallel the edge at a fixed offset.
Small camera-y jitter across data renders to break the perfectly symmetric mouth-centered composition (no scene edit needed).
Keep pairing with batch1 decoys (N1 shadow band, D4 subway platform) so darkness and furniture shortcuts are penalized by counterexamples.

scenes.drop_type: levee crest shoulder -> stair cut through slope: 20 steps x 0.16 m (3.2 m drop), unguarded (no railing by identity), water-anchored
scenes.drop_summary: T5 identity: no railing x water anchor. The stair and the slope fold vanish completely from low viewpoints; the drop is evidenced only by what lies below and beyond - the promenade with white cycle-track lines, benches, poplars rooted below eye level, and the teal river. The paved crest walk ends at x=-1.0 with a protected 1.0 m grass shoulder before the true edge at x=0, which itself shows zero contrast (grass fold). At h0.3_d5 and h0.3_d10 the water and everything below the crest are occluded and the scene reads as a flat park - the drop is essentially uncued there.

cues.notes: The true crest shoulder (x=0) is a grass-on-grass fold with no measurable line in any preset. The only visible line is the clay-paving river edge at x=-1.0 (paving L 174-179 warm vs far strip L 99-150) - 1.0 m BEFORE the drop; treating it as the edge is a built-in mislocalization trap.

Across the hidden fold the far surface is the promenade dirt band (L 155+-42, RGB 164/156/123) or water (L 126) 3.2-3.6 m below - visible at d2 (all heights) and h1.8_d5. Where occluded, the visible sequence paving->grass->tree crowns is indistinguishable from a flat park.
No shadow marks the fold; only tree/bollard/bench cast shadows on crest and promenade.

Where the sightline clears the crest (d2 rows, h1.8_d5) the below-grade world is rich: promenade with functional white lane lines (L 183 vs 156 dirt), benches, poplars whose trunks are cut by the crest (crowns below eye height), then water and the far bank. At h0.9_d5/d10 and h1.8_d10 it thins to a water band; at h0.3_d5/d10 nothing below the crest is visible at all.
cue_nosing=False; uniform-riser marking declined by GT-46/47 ruling (zero visual return - the stair is invisible from the approach anyway). Stair treads appear in none of the 9 presets.
Not levee practice; config key reserved only.
No railing anywhere near the edge - the scene's research identity (G3 timber post-and-rail fence explicitly DECLINED). The one-pipe stair rail option (cue_railing=True) is off by default.
Flush grass shoulder at the edge. The grey soldier-course edging between turf and clay paving (visible in d10 frames) is flat and sits >1 m before the edge.

Genuine below-grade evidence: slope shrub beds (real USD shrubs) whose crowns peek over the crest at the corridor flanks (d5/d10), and poplar crowns rising from the promenade with trunk bases hidden (d2/d5). At h0.3_d10 the crowns read equally well as bushes standing on flat ground - ambiguous.

THE anchor cue. Teal band RGB (96,133,138), L~126; chromatic inversion vs paving (paving R-B = +42, water B-R = +42). Wide at h0.3_d2/h0.9_d2/h1.8_d2/h1.8_d5, present at h0.9_d5/h1.8_d10, a sliver at h0.9_d10 - and fully ABSENT at h0.3_d5 and h0.3_d10, exactly the presets where every other cue also fails.

No edge signage (cue_sign=False). Indirect markings: white cycle-track lane lines on the promenade below (dL ~27 over dirt; functional road markings, visible with the promenade at d2 rows + h1.8_d5) and the red/white river gauge pole standing in the water in most frames - both mark the lower world, not the edge.

Water is the scene's only smooth surface (tower reflections at h0.9_d2 right, dark reflection under the overpass); at noon it renders mostly as flat teal, so the specular signature is mild and exactly co-extensive with water visibility.

Bollard pair at the spur edge (cy +-1.2) frames the stair mouth at d5/d10; two small paving notches at the crest edge mark the spur at d10; the overpass deck descends into the right frame edge; the far bank rises behind the water. The fold itself never breaks the skyline (towers fill it).

shortcut_risks: Teal-band shortcut: 'water above the pavement = drop'. It is the dominant cue wherever present and absent exactly at h0.3_d5/d10 - a model keyed to it fails at grazing far range and false-fires on any visible water without a near drop.

Paving-edge mislocalization: the clay->grass line at x=-1.0 is the only crisp line in most frames; learning it as the edge places the boundary 1.0 m early (GT edge is the zero-contrast grass fold at x=0).
'Bollard pair = stair mouth' furniture proxy (the pair appears nowhere else on the crest walk).
Red/white gauge pole co-occurrence: pole in frame = river = drop.
Scene-identity binding: the herringbone clay paving texture is unique to scene03 in the library - texture alone can stand in for 'drop ahead at a fixed distance'.
Crowns-above-crest evidence is ambiguous at h0.3_d10 (reads as hedges on flat ground) - it can teach the opposite lesson if unsupported.
suggestions: Worn crest lip: a 0.15-0.3 m band of worn/sparse turf tone along the shoulder fold at x~0 (mowing and foot wear on levee shoulders is standard) - the only realistic edge-bound ground cue that survives h0.3 grazing; keeps the protected 1.0 m grass shoulder geometry untouched.

Raise height variance of the existing slope shrubs so 1-2 crowns break the crest line by 10-20 cm within the judged corridor flanks - below-grade vegetation evidence that persists when the water is occluded (assets already owned; no new species).
Darken the stair-head CrestBand course/joints one tone step (a functional stair-head course, not a decorative rectangle) so the mouth reads at d5 where today only the bollards mark it.

Data-mix countermeasures: render camera-yaw arms where the river leaves the frame laterally, and pair with batch1 decoys (N2 asphalt patch, N1 shadow band) so teal/darkness shortcuts are punished by counterexamples.
Decouple the bollard proxy by repeating the same bollard model at ordinary intervals along the crest walk (normal levee furniture) - verify against the 03-B bollard ruling first.
Vary the river gauge pole's station along the bank between renders (it is a water marker, not fixed furniture) to remove its fixed co-occurrence with the stair corridor.

scenes.drop_type: switchback timber deck stair on a park slope (4 flights x 10 open-riser steps, riser 0.165/tread 0.30, total drop 6.60 m) plus an unguarded 30-degree grass side slope (south of trail shoulder y<-1.6, -2.3 m within 4 m)
scenes.drop_summary: Grid origin (0,0,0) at the deck entry off a dirt/grass park trail; approach presets look +X along the trail into the deck head. Registered drop 6.600 m over guarded flights/landings; by 08-05 doctrine the continuous guard IS the drop cue (broken_landing=None). Open risers + a leaf-litter band over treads 1-2 deliberately erase the nosing line. SCENE_CONFIG: cue_railing=True, cue_material_break=True, cue_tactile/nosing/sign=False.

cues.notes: By design: open risers give no tread/riser light-dark pair and the leaf band bites treads 1-2, so the first nosing never forms a line. Measured at h0.3_d10 the distant deck strip vs ground band directly below it is Michelson 0.015 (L 136.4 vs 140.6) - invisible. At h0.9+/d2 the board-end line reads only against through-baluster green (deck L 182.8 vs far grass L 92.0, M 0.33).

Neutral-grey weathered timber (L~183, RGB 186/183/177) vs strongly green-chroma lower-park grass/leaf ground (L 92-140, G-dominant). Reads wherever the far side is visible (h0.9/h1.8, and through balusters at h0.3_d2); at h0.3_d5/d10 the far side only appears above the floor line so the change is not 'across the edge'.

Baluster shadow lattice crosses the deck at the guarded edge: lit deck 182.8 vs shadow 137.1 (M 0.143) at h0.3_d2; 187.7 vs 118.6 (M 0.226) at h0.9_d2. Marks the guard line, not the void itself; too small/distant at d10 presets.

Lower park trail, rocks, hedge crowns, leafless trees and the next flight's railing are visible below deck level at h0.9/h1.8; at h0.3_d2 the lower-flight rail run and green slope show through baluster gaps (M 0.33 vs deck). At h0.3_d5/d10 depth collapses to a backdrop slope behind the rail (railing vs slope M only 0.047) and could read as level ground.
cue_nosing=False - a nosing band on a park timber deck is not the practice (code path reserved only).
cue_tactile=False - not the practice on a park dirt trail (v5 brief); code path only.

THE dominant cue (08-05 doctrine): continuous square-sawn 방부목 guard h1.10, 38x38 balusters @0.30 clear, capped 90x90 newels, inside O35 handrail; every landing edge guarded (broken_landing=None), rake rails on every flight. Visible in all 9 presets; at h0.3_d10 only as a low-contrast silhouette vs the olive slope (L 103.0 vs 93.8, M 0.047) - geometry, not luminance, carries it.

90x90 경계목 timber edging flanks the approach trail as two converging lines pointing at the deck head - a path-boundary/leading-line cue, not an upstand at any drop edge; the deck edges themselves have no kick or curb.

Entry shrubs pin the break line of the unguarded 30% south slope (hazard cue 4) but that slope never enters the preset corridor. Ridge-crest hedge crowns appear near eye level beyond the deck at h0.9+/h1.8 (valley hint). The leaf-litter band on treads 1-2 is an ANTI-cue: it hides the first nosing so the deck entry reads flat.
No water in scene.
cue_sign=False (v5.2 user: arbitrary warning signs removed). The timber waymarker (directional blades) is navigation dressing, off the judged axis.
Matte weathered timber, matte grass/dirt, no wet surfaces - no exploitable specular discontinuity in any preset.

The zigzag itself: descending rake rails, stepped newel caps, four flights and landings stacked downhill are legible at d5/d10 (h0.9/h1.8) as a structure sinking below the horizon; at h0.3_d2 only the near balustrade and one rake are in frame. NOTE an artifact rides this cue: a flat untextured grey plate (L~90, zero texture - the uncovered cavity/backdrop gap at the slope base) is visible left of the structure in h0.9_d2, h1.8_d2 and h1.8_d10.

shortcut_risks: Railing<->drop is 1:1 inside the preset corridor: the scene's own counterexample (unguarded 30-degree south slope) never appears in a judged frame, so a rail-keyed model is never contradicted
Flat untextured grey plate (backdrop/cavity gap at the slope base, L~90) is visible adjacent to the drop structure in h0.9_d2/h1.8_d2/h1.8_d10 - a synthetic 'void grey = drop' token
Leaf litter is concentrated at the stair head (treads 1-2 + entry) - leaves become a proxy for the hidden edge
Material split: neutral-grey timber = hazard zone, green grass = safe ground
Scattered white rocks appear only on the approach trail in judged frames - 'rocks = corridor before a drop' correlation
suggestions: Close the grey backdrop gap: extend the rock_face/lower terrain plate so no untextured void-grey plate abuts the drop structure (pure artifact fix, no drop-edge move)
Darken the rim joist/fascia board at the deck entry with a realistic weathering band so h0.3 gets a genuine edge line (current grazing line contrast M~0.015) without touching geometry
De-correlate leaves from the edge: drift a few leaf patches onto mid-flight treads and onto flat deck areas away from the head (keeps the treads-1-2 research cue, removes 'leaf=edge')
Add training crops (not new presets) that frame the unguarded south slope - a drop with no railing - to break the rail<->drop shortcut with existing geometry
Give the backdrop slope and ridge hedge crowns mild albedo variation so far-side depth reads by texture gradient at grazing instead of by the flat-olive fill

scenes.drop_type: steel footbridge (H-plan) deck-end/tower-head free edge: 5.505 m to the sidewalk at x=15.00; east mid landings 2.755 m with no kickplate (control pair on west); grating treads with see-through slits
scenes.drop_summary: Preset grid origin (15.00, 0, 5.50) = the east head landing's outer edge met head-on by a deck-crossing robot; approach corridor is the deck itself. Hazard premise: at h0.3 the balustrade lower band is open-ish but the parapet/kick wall means the far sidewalk shows only as skyline and 'the floor reads as continuous'. cue_railing/nosing/material_break/sign=True, cue_tactile=False. Cue toggles never move drop transforms.

cues.notes: The only floor-level line in the corridor is the landing-floor-to-guard-kick junction: L 203.4 vs 196.9, Michelson 0.016, parapet face std 0.7 - beige-on-beige, effectively invisible. The true free edge is behind the parapet in every preset; no preset shows a floor-to-void line.

Beyond the guard the content flips to lawn/hedge (landing floor L 199.2 vs lawn L 117.5, M 0.258 at h1.8_d5), but the near ground band below the edge is fully occluded by the parapet, so it reads as wall-then-garden rather than floor-then-void. Along-path texture change (ribbed grating strip vs smooth deck, M 0.049 but std 18.7 vs 3.5) marks 'on the bridge', not the edge.

Baluster shadow ladders rake across the deck and landing (right side of h0.3_d2, both flanks at h0.9_d10/h1.8_d10) and anchor the guard line; the deck's own cast shadow on the roadway is visible only in mise-en-scene cuts, never in presets.

Two forms: (a) skyline cue at every preset - street-hedge crowns and lawn appear AT deck height over the parapet (ground objects at eye level implies elevation); (b) through the flank balusters at h0.9_d10/h1.8_d10 the below-deck world is directly visible (lawn, sidewalk, road with double-yellow centreline, the descending flight). Dead-ahead at h0.3 nothing below deck level is visible - the concealment premise holds, so this cue carries no positive evidence exactly where judging happens.

cue_nosing=True: yellow non-slip bands on every grating tread; measured through the left balustrade at h0.9_d10 ~0.4% of a 520x230 crop, mean RGB (206,198,92) - high-hue, tiny area, oblique only. The judged deck-end drop has no stair, so the nosing never marks the primary hazard; it evidences 'a level change nearby'.
cue_tactile=False by v5.2 user ruling (rare in reality); ablation code path kept.

Continuous beige balustrade: statutory 0.100 m clear balusters, kick band 0.16, guard runs with kick wall on landings, one ribbon height 1.25 (GT-96); present and dominant in all 9 presets. The east mid landings' missing kickplate (hazard 2, 2.755 m) is the research variable and sits outside the preset corridor (midlanding cut only).

The kick band/parapet at every edge is a real upstand marking the boundary - but it is simultaneously the occluder that hides the drop at h0.3 (the double role is why edge contrast is 0.016). Roadway kerb 0.15 (S06-B) exists below, visible only in mise-en-scene cuts.

Street hedge masses + trees line the sidewalk; their crowns form the persistent over-parapet skyline at every preset (hedge band L 139.5 vs brick 127.5, M 0.045 - chroma carries it, not luminance). The hedges are smooth untextured green domes (near-zero albedo variation) - synthetic-looking, which converts this honest cue into a spurious token.
No water in scene.

cue_sign=True: two Korean guidance signs (0.90x0.60) stand at the stair feet, facing approaching pedestrians - occluded in ALL 9 presets (below deck, behind towers). Road lane paint (double-yellow centre, white dashes) is visible one level down through the flank balusters at h0.9_d10/h1.8_d10 - markings-below-you as a depth hint.
Painted steel at 0.30 rough/0.25 metallic reads matte at noon; facade windows are far-field flat blue. No specular discontinuity marks the edge.

Rake rails descending at the deck flanks (left of h0.3_d10), the towers' stair boxes, deck piers, and in stair_head the balustrade lines converging on open sky beyond the outer guard. At d2 presets the silhouette reduces to the near guard geometry alone.

shortcut_risks: Beige pipe balustrade + kick band <-> drop is 1:1: no other beige-railed structure exists, so guard vocabulary alone predicts the label
Flat untextured green hedge domes over a low wall = 'you are high' - the depth cue is carried by a synthetic-looking flat-albedo token a CNN can key on
Yellow = stairs/hazard: yellow pixels occur only on tread nosings and the road centreline
Ribbed grating strip underfoot = 'on the footbridge' = drop ahead (location token independent of any edge evidence)
Brick facade filling the upper frame co-occurs with every elevated judged frame (backdrop-as-label correlation)
suggestions: Give the parapet foot a realistic grime/water-stain line and the kick band a slightly darker cap so the floor-to-guard junction rises from M 0.016 toward ~0.1 at h0.3 - dirt accumulation at a wall foot is standard footbridge reality, zero geometry moved
Add albedo/texture variation to the hedge domes and backdrop lawn (port scene10's tinted-crown treatment) so far-side depth reads as vegetation texture, not as a flat green blob token

Place short pedestrian guard-fence segments (보행자 방호울타리) on the sidewalk around the stair feet - standard Korean roadside practice - creating rail-without-drop counterexamples in below-deck views without touching the deck vocabulary
Within the one-ribbon guard doctrine (GT-96), allow mild per-bay paint weathering (chips/rust bloom at post bases) so the guard is not one uniform beige token everywhere
Keep cue_tactile=False as ruled, but run the reserved tactile ablation arm in a variant batch so the trainee sees the stair-head cue class somewhere in the corpus

scenes.drop_type: waterfront cantilever timber deck: one-sided concealed 1.80 m drop past the river-side rail (deck 0.00 to water -1.80 over hidden riprap band y 1.25-8.75) + 8-riser 1.36 m stair at the deck end (x=0) to the lower floodplain
scenes.drop_summary: Travel axis +X ends at the stair head x=0; river is +Y (left in presets). By GT-43/GT-66 the guard is Ø120 posts with two Ø80 log rails, no infill, no kick - the h0.3 sight line running out UNDER the mid rail is the scene's negative-obstacle premise: the near water/riprap band vanishes and water appears glued to the deck edge. Deck L* recalibrated (GT-44) to L*55/albedo 0.229. cue_railing/material_break=True; nosing/tactile/sign=False.

cues.notes: Deck-end line at h0.3_d2: deck rows L 179.3 vs the band beyond L 102.6 - Michelson 0.272, crisp. But it collapses with distance at grazing: at h0.3_d10 deck-end rows 130.0 vs rows beyond 131.4, M 0.005 - the line is luminance-invisible and only a slight chroma shift (B 112 vs 141) remains. River-side edge vs wet riprap measures M 0.239 (edge_void cut) yet that band is hidden below the sight line at all h0.3 presets.

Pale timber (RGB 185/178/170) flips to teal water (107/135/143, M 0.169 + large hue shift), lower lawn (M 0.250), dark brick revetment paving (94.0 vs 179.3, M 0.31). Reads at every preset >= h0.9 and at h0.3_d2; compressed to a few pixel rows at h0.3_d10.

Noon front-light along +X: no cast shadow marks the deck end in any preset; tread shadows appear only in the stair_join side cut; bench shadows on the lower lawn (h0.9+/h1.8) weakly hint the second, lower ground plane.

Water at -1.8, stepped riprap tiers, lower lawn with benches, bike path - all visibly beyond/below the deck at h0.9/h1.8 (riprap tiers read as descending ledges left of centre); still strong at h0.3_d2. At h0.3_d10 depth compresses to a thin far band; the reed TIPS poking above the deck-end line are then the clearest depth break. The 7.5 m near band (riprap+water y 1.25-8.75) is hidden at all h0.3 presets - the declared concealment.
cue_nosing=False (key reserved). Stair treads are plain timber; at grazing the whole flight hides below the deck-end line.
cue_tactile=False - not customary on a waterfront timber deck; code path reserved.

Continuous river-side round-log guard (Ø120 posts @1.5 m, two Ø80 rails at 1.10, no pickets, no kick - GT-66 reinstated): the doctrine cue 'water beyond the rail'. Deliberately open under the mid rail so the h0.3 sight line exits below it (research premise - do not infill). One-sided: no guard at the stair (walking route) or the level south edge - correct practice, and it keeps rail-presence from being a global drop token within the scene.
Boards run flush to the free edge; no kick plate or edge beam upstand by declaration (GT-43/GT-66).

Reed/silver-grass stands (164-stalk bands, v7 item 2) mark the shoreline in every preset; at h0.3_d10 their tips are the only vertical elements crossing the deck-end line (real depth break). The 1:2 grass slope flanks the stair as the walkable detour.

Teal water plane fills the left third at every preset - unmistakable 'river beyond'. But it is nearly textureless (edge_void water crop std 1.4 despite rough 0.14): a mirror-flat synthetic region; and at h0.3 the water visually starts AT the deck edge because the riprap band is hidden, so the water cue signals presence of a drop while concealing its 1.80 m scale (the premise).

No signs (cue_sign=False, v5.2 ruling; GT-115 also deleted the stray bollards). The bike path's white edge lines on the lower floodplain are the only markings - visible from h0.3_d2 upward, they tag the second ground plane.

Wet tide band on the riprap crest (edge_void: dark olive sheen, L 89.2, sparkle std 38.4 vs deck 26.8) marks the waterline; visible only obliquely/from h0.9+ on the left flank - hidden below the h0.3 sight line.

Backdrop bridge piers rise from the water with their bases cut off by the deck edge (occlusion implies the deck overhangs a void); benches seen top-down on the lower lawn at h0.9+; stair form and deck fascia/log piles legible only in mise-en-scene cuts (stair_join, bank_face, under_deck).

shortcut_risks: Teal flat plane at frame-left <-> drop scene: water position and color are constant in every corridor view
Round-log post-and-rail vocabulary appears only at the water edge - rail style alone predicts 'water drop'
Reed stalks = edge nearby (reeds exist only in the shoreline band)
Benches and white-lined bike path occur exclusively on the lower level - 'street furniture = below' correlation
Synthetic-flatness token: far lawn and water are near-zero-texture regions (water std 1.4) while walkable surfaces are textured - 'flat region = far/lower' shortcut
At h0.3_d10 the stair drop has no local evidence (edge M 0.005), so a model can only get it right by keying on global context (water left, reeds) - context-only prediction masquerading as detection
suggestions: Realistic end-grain/weathering darkening on the deck-end board and first stair nosing so the grazing edge line survives distance (M 0.005 -> >0.05 at h0.3_d10) with no added strip or geometry move

Within the ruled water_rough band (0.14, scene09 0.15 family), add mild normal/ripple detail near the shoreline so the water is not a zero-texture mirror region - restores a texture-gradient depth cue and weakens the flat-region shortcut
Place one bench on the upper promenade band (south of the deck, z 0) so benches stop being an exclusive lower-level marker

A few extra rubble stones breaking the waterline silhouette beyond y 3.9 (outside the concealed band) - riprap irregularity is realistic and gives grazing views a second vertical break like the reed tips, without touching the y 1.25-8.75 hidden-band premise
Mow-band or patchy albedo variation on the lower lawn so the lower plane reads as textured ground rather than a flat green fill

scenes.drop_type: T7 fan winder — 12 radial steps (r_in 1.2 / r_out 4.0, riser 0.15, total drop 1.8 m) descending from a rooftop membrane deck (z0) to a lower terrace (−1.95), entry throat at x≈3.46–4.0 / y 0–2
scenes.drop_summary: Judged presets (h{0.3,0.9,1.8} x d{2,3.5,5}, mirrored about x=5.8) look across the green urethane deck toward the L-core; the eye is 9.6–13.1 m from the drop edge. Every fan tread and the whole descent are self-occluded behind the deck lip at all 9 presets; the drop is evidenced only by the deck-end material break (green membrane -> grey threshold slabs), the L-core shadow wedge over the entry, and low guard walls that read as generic rooftop furniture. The stair itself is only legible in the mise-en-scene cuts (winder_mid, entry_gate, lower_lookup, radial_nosing).

cues.notes: The true drop line (first radial nosing arc at the entry) is occluded at ALL 9 presets — the sightline clears the deck lip by <0.15 m even at h1.8_d2 (slope 1.8/12.6=0.143), so at most a sliver of the kite landing could show and in the renders none does. The only visible line is the deck-lip joint 0.5–1.3 m BEFORE the drop: sunlit deck lum 0.68 vs sunlit threshold slabs 0.71 (4% step; chroma carries it: G−R +0.088 vs 0.00). In the core shadow the slabs read 0.13 — the line flips polarity depending on shadow position.

Ribbed green urethane membrane (roll seams at 1.0 m pitch, groove texture) against smooth grey concrete slabs is the strongest preset cue, but it is a PROXY 0.5–1.3 m before the actual nosing line, not the drop edge itself. At h0.3_d3.5/d5 the slab band compresses to a <10 px grazing sliver.

The L-core (crown 2.55+0.12) throws a hard shadow wedge over the entry threshold in every preset: shadowed slabs lum 0.13 vs sunlit deck 0.68 (5.2x). It reliably marks the entry ZONE but is cast by the wall, not the drop — a lighting-bound, ambiguous cue (finding L19-F1: the winder corridor gets sky light only; GT-82 restored only ~50% of the landing to sun).

Through the stair opening: no lower surface is ever visible at the presets (fully self-occluded). Indirect depth exists at h0.9/h1.8 frame-right — the lower terrace (−1.95) parapet band and its membrane turn-up visible beyond the roof perimeter parapet ('another level below'), and it vanishes at h0.3. Full far-side depth (lower plaza pavers) appears only in winder_mid / lower_lookup cuts.
cue_nosing=False (SCENE_CONFIG); radial anti-slip arc bands exist only as an ablation path. Tread arrises are bare stone; even those are preset-invisible.
cue_tactile=False by ruling (§12.4 — private rooftop, not covered by the accessibility act; path kept for ablation only).

Edge-guard retaining wall (x 3.46–4.0, y 2–4, h 1.1), outer arc parapet ring on sectors 4–8 (h 1.1 + handrail band), end piers with gate-post finials (GT-82(4), cap at pier+0.30). At the presets the guard wall and pier finial ARE visible (h0.9/h1.8) but read as generic rooftop walls among the perimeter parapets; the descending arc ring — the element that actually encodes a stair — is hidden behind the edge guard from the preset axis. At h0.3 nothing resolves.

Rooftop perimeter parapets with green membrane turn-up (h 1.2 / inner 1.1) frame the whole deck — they signal 'this is a roof, edges drop 6 m' as context, but there is deliberately no upstand at the stair threshold itself.
Only the west-end rooftop planter (juniper crown enters h1.8_d5 frame corner). No vegetation relates to the drop.
Drain water marks are flat 0.6 mm-class stains around the two roof drains; no standing water, no depth signal.
cue_sign reserved/False; no painted markings. (Deck roll seams and 2 recoat patches are maintenance vocabulary, not markings.)
GT-115 gloss ladder exists on the DECK (field spec 0.25 chalked vs recoat 0.60 fresh) — visible as sheen patches near the drains, unrelated to the drop. No specular event at the drop edge.

Roofscape grammar carries an inference: rooftop door beside the only paved throat + pier finial + the deck ending against open sky at frame right. The winder's own silhouette (descending ring crowns) never breaks the preset skyline.

shortcut_risks: 'green membrane ends -> drop': the grey slab band at the deck lip is the only slab paving in the judged frames, and it sits 0.5-1.3 m BEFORE the true nosing line — a detector will localize the wrong line and learn material-transition = hazard
'dark shadow wedge beside the door = drop': the L-core shadow covers the entry at noon in every round (structural, L19-F1) — a lighting artifact standing in for the hazard
'rooftop door + gate post = stair here': scene grammar makes the only door co-occur with the only descent
position prior: at every preset the drop evidence sits in the same upper-center/right band of frame at 9.6-13.1 m — distance and framing never vary the cue set
suggestions: Lay standard roof-membrane walk pads (grey pads on the green field) as a maintenance path from the rooftop door across the deck toward the drains — decorrelates 'grey paving on green = stair threshold' with completely ordinary roof practice

Run occasional rounds with the existing cue_nosing ablation arm ON (worn safety-yellow radial arcs per GT-114 band, alb <= 0.50): gives the entry a second, on-edge carrier without new vocabulary; plausible for a publicly-walked corner winder
Add a small slab equipment apron in front of the HVAC/vent run (standard practice) so slab paving also occurs away from the drop
Schedule an alternate sun-azimuth round (morning) so the entry corridor is not always inside the core shadow — breaks the shadow-wedge co-occurrence the noon-only lighting bakes in

scenes.drop_type: T8 diagonal oblique — straight 14-step flight (riser 0.15, tread 0.34, width 5.0, drop 2.1 m) rotated 30 deg to the walk axis; mesa plaza (z0) over a grass valley (−2.15) with a sunken lower corridor (−2.1)
scenes.drop_summary: Presets h{0.3,0.9,1.8} x d{2,5,10} look +X while the drop line runs x=−0.577y across the frame. The flight itself is self-occluded at every preset; since GT-87 the drop is guarded by two masonry cheek walls whose descending wedge silhouettes (concrete face lum 0.35–0.37, band_dark coping 0.29–0.32) are visible at ALL 9 presets and are the only evidence at h0.3. Near-field (h0.9_d2) the drop-edge hairline is strong (min-lum 0.19 vs paving 0.77); the mesa lip against valley grass (0.7 vs 0.44 + hue) carries the line at h0.9/h1.8; the lower corridor with bench/bollards is visible at h1.8 d5/d10 as true far-side depth.

cues.notes: Two carriers: (1) the drop-edge hairline (first-riser gap/shade) — measured min-lum 0.19 against 0.77 paving at h0.9_d2 near field; sub-pixel by d5–d10; never visible at h0.3 (grazing); (2) the mesa-lip line against valley grass — pavement ~0.70 vs grass 0.44 (1.6x + green hue), visible h0.9/h1.8, a thin band at h0.3_d2/d5, gone at h0.3_d10. Note the visible lip line over most of the frame is the CLIFF edge to grass, not the stair — the walkable drop between the walls shows the weakest line.

Three-way break: plaza_light 600-unit flags + dark granite inlay bands (upper) / grass (valley below the lip) / plaza_lower warm small-unit pavers (corridor floor, scale 2.4). The clipped band ends stepping along the diagonal also encode the boundary orientation (the W2-D clamp turned a defect into a theme cue).

Noon shadows fall away from the camera; no broad shadow band marks the void. The h0.9_d2 hairline is part shadow; the near cheek wall's shaded inner face (0.35–0.37 vs 0.77 sunlit paving) forms a dark wedge that flags the stair slot indirectly.

The sunken corridor entrance (plaza_lower + 4-bollard row w/ yellow bands + bench) is visible beyond/below the lip at h0.9_d5 (left apron), h1.8_d5/d10 and the along_diagonal cut — reduced object scale plus T-junction truncation at the lip. Blocked by the near cheek wall at d2 and fully lost at h0.3.
cue_nosing key reserved; bare stone arrises. Treads are preset-invisible anyway (self-occluded).
OFF by identity ruling (§12.4 hidden illusion; gate B12 _inv_hidden_illusion refuses tactile or any bright albedo>0.28 full-width transverse line for scene20).

GT-87 masonry cheek walls both flanks (wall_h 0.95 + coping 0.06 = 1.01 m guard line over the nosing), band_dark coping reads as a dark descending LINE at 20 m (coping 0.29–0.32 vs wall 0.35 vs sky/grass). Visible at every one of the 9 presets — at h0.3_d10 the two wedge profiles above the horizon are effectively the only drop evidence in frame.
The open diagonal mesa lip outside the flight width is a bare arris straight to the grass slope — no curb. (Wall newel heads counted under railing_or_guard.)

Valley grass abuts the lip over the left half of every frame; tree trunk bases and brick building bases sit 2.15 m below mesa level (bases occluded at low h = depth inference). At h0.3 the grass compresses to a horizon band.
None.
cue_sign False (v5.2 ruling). Bollard yellow reflective bands exist but sit at the plaza vehicle entry and the lower corridor entrance, not at the drop line.
Matte granite/grass at noon; no specular discontinuity across the edge worth measuring.

The descending wedge profile of each cheek wall + high square newel head is a direct icon of 'stair going down', readable even at h0.3_d10 where every surface cue has vanished. The staircase-clipped dark band terminations echo the 30 deg boundary.

shortcut_risks: 'concrete wedge wall with dark coping = drop': the cheek walls occur nowhere else in the scene and are the sole h0.3 evidence — the cue_railing=False ablation arm at h0.3 is nearly drop-free, so a model trained on default arms can lean entirely on the walls
'pavement-to-grass boundary = falling ground': every open mesa edge in this scene drops 2.15 m to the valley, so grass adjacency is a perfect (spurious) drop predictor in-scene
'dark transverse granite band = approaching edge': the last inlay band sits ~1 m before the drop on the axis; band spacing gives a countdown prior
composition prior: the drop always enters from the right half of frame as a falling-to-the-left diagonal (fixed 30 deg + fixed preset axis)
suggestions: Add a linear trench grate along the stair-head crest (the declared storm line already drains to the north stair-head gully — KDS trigger table supports a head drain at a sunken flight): an on-edge, guard-independent texture cue that survives the cue_railing ablation arm

Introduce one paving-to-lawn transition WITHOUT a drop at mesa level (flush turf parterre inset near the bollard row, a common civic-plaza feature) so grass adjacency stops being a perfect drop predictor

Repeat the wall vocabulary away from the drop: a low freestanding seat wall in the same masonry + band_dark coping along the plaza's north side breaks the 'wedge wall = drop' uniqueness while staying inside the G1 civic furniture register

Within the GT-126 trace-litter ruling, bias a few of the existing flakes into the stair-head reentrant corner (wind-drift catch line) — a subtle organic accumulation exactly at the void that adds an independent near-edge cue at h0.9/h1.8

scenes.drop_type: T2 monumental grand stair — 18 steps (riser 0.15, tread 0.32, width 8, effective 7, drop 2.7 m) from a marble terrace to a granite grand plaza; multi-step self-occlusion is the scene identity
scenes.drop_summary: Presets h{0.3,0.9,1.8} x d{2,5,10} approach along the terrace axis; the lower 16-18 steps fold behind the crest at every preset and the lower plaza reads nearly coplanar with the terrace (crest seam: marble lum 0.82 vs plaza 0.79, a 4% step carried mostly by warm->cool chroma, R-B +0.047 -> -0.05). The 18 worn-yellow nosing strips are complete but invisible from the whole judged grid (no yellow signal at the seam rows; first strip below frame at d2) — exactly the scene's 'fittings complete but powerless' thesis. The two stainless baluster railings (y ±1.3) with their crest head-frames, plus the stone parapet newel wedges at d5/d10, are the only robust preset evidence; the dark granite axis wear-lane (lum 0.48 vs marble 0.61, ending 0.85 m before the crest) forms an unintended runway pointing at the drop in all 9 frames.

cues.notes: Crest seam measured at h0.3_d2: marble band 0.818 vs plaza 0.787 sRGB lum (1.04x); the real carrier is chroma (R-B +0.047 marble vs -0.05 plaza — a 0.1 warm/cool swing). Single-pixel transition row at d10 (seam rows 313–342 across presets); no dark seam line (no shadow at the crest).

Warm large marble flags vs cooler plaza_light with a denser joint grid; the abrupt joint-spacing/perspective-density jump across the seam is a genuine monocular depth discontinuity at h0.9/h1.8, fully compressed at h0.3.

By design: SUN_AZ_OFFSET 206.5 pulled shadows off the axis (v5 foreground-crush fix); riser shadows fold away with the treads; measured seam rows show no luminance dip. Flagpole/streetlight shadows cross the terrace but never mark the crest.

Lower plaza visible in all frames with benches, trace litter, and band_dark strips whose trapezoids are TRUNCATED by the invisible crest (clean T-junctions at h1.8_d2 bottom); grass band and backdrop bases beyond. But white-on-white tonality makes it read as continuation — the depth interpretation is anchored by the railings, not the surfaces.

cue_nosing=True — 18 worn safety-yellow strips (GT-114 color, 0.05 m wide, front arris of each tread). Occluded at ALL 9 judged presets: yellowness scan at the crest rows shows no spike (0.010–0.033 transition vs 0.044 marble baseline); at d2 the first strip is below the frame's -28 deg bottom edge. Vivid only in the railing_line down-view (and lower-plaza return cuts).
OFF by identity ruling (B12 _inv_hidden_illusion enforces it for scene21).

Two stainless baluster railing lines (y ±1.3, rail_h 0.9, metallic 0.9) with 0.5 m terrace back-extensions: their head-frames stand AT the crest and the runs descend below the terrace plane — visible in all 9 presets (frame-edge at d2, fully in-frame at d5/d10). Stone parapet newel wedges (±3.5–4.0, +0.85) add mass at d5/d10. This ensemble is the scene's sole robust preset cue.
Flush marble arris at the crest; no upstand anywhere on the drop line.
Grass band + L21 tree rows behind the lower plaza; trunk bases at −2.7ish level partially occluded by the crest — context depth only, 20+ m past the edge.
None (axis 'water staining' is a dry tone lane — see signage/shortcut notes).

One sign_info at (−3.2, −5.4): behind the d2 eye and >29 deg off-axis at d5/d10 — outside every judged frame (contributes only to non-judged cuts). No painted hazard markings by ruling. The dark granite axis wear-lane functions as a de-facto marking (see shortcut_risks).
Stainless rails (rough 0.35) throw bright specular verticals/diagonals at the crest — a sub-cue of the railing ensemble. Marble vs plaza sheen difference is negligible at preset angles.

Parapet newel wedges + railing head-frames break the horizon at d5/d10; the joint-grid density discontinuity at the seam doubles as a silhouette-class cue. Obelisk/flagpoles/streetlights are context verticals only.

shortcut_risks: 'twin descending stainless railings = drop': no other railing exists in the scene; with nosings preset-invisible and the seam at 4% luminance, cue_railing=False frames are essentially drop-free — the model can bind entirely to the railing

'dark granite axis runway ends -> crest 0.85 m ahead': the wear lane measures lum 0.48 vs 0.61 marble (21% step) with crisp tile-like edges and appears dead-center in all 9 presets — far stronger than a water stain and a perfect distance-to-edge proxy
'warm cream -> neutral white paving seam = drop line' (chroma shortcut that would break on same-stone plazas)
fixed furniture priors: manhole disc pair at x=−4 flanking the axis and the parapet newel wedges at the frame edges always co-occur with the crest at fixed offsets
suggestions: Re-tune the axis wear-lane toward its declared identity (water staining, not inlay): feather the edges and cut the albedo delta roughly in half (target <= ~10% vs marble, irregular boundary) — improves realism and defuses the strongest unintended axis shortcut in one move

Add a worn-arris band on the crest itself: a ~5 cm slightly DARKER, smoother wear line along the top step edge (foot-polished stone; darker not brighter, so it stays clear of the B12 bright-transverse-line gate) — gives h0.9/h1.8 a true on-edge line that survives railing ablation

Lay one band_dark apron strip on the lower plaza at the stair foot (standard grand-stair detail): every preset then contains a clean, high-contrast T-junction truncated by the crest, strengthening the far-side depth reading without touching the crest
Keep periodic cue_railing=False ablation rounds paired with the two edge-line reinforcements above, so edge localization has non-railing support at every h

scenes.drop_type: T20 canopy-shadow underpass stair: 20x0.15m flight (3.0m drop, run 6.40m) descending from plaza z=0 at edge x=0 into a covered passage (z=-3.00) under a 6-lane road; canopy roof z=2.6 casts its shadow along +X over the whole flight. Secondary registered drop: 150mm road kerbs at x=7.80/13.80.
scenes.drop_summary: Pit reads as a near-black void in a bright paver plaza. Flight surface is self-occluded at ALL 9 presets (grazing rays blocked by the rim at h0.3/h0.9; below the -10deg-pitch frame or under the sight envelope at h1.8), so the drop is evidenced by the rim line, the statutory yellow head tactile band, railings, and the visible passage floor at depth - never by the steps themselves.

cues.notes: Paver field (central-third row-mean L ~190-200/255) terminates in a near-black trench: profile minima L=5-9 at d2/d5, Michelson ~0.94. Dark fraction (L<40): 35.9% at h0.9_d2, 27.8% h1.8_d2, 19.4% h0.3_d2, shrinking to 3-6% at d10. At h1.8_d2 the rim itself sits at 42deg depression, below the frame bottom (28deg) - only the trench interior/far wall is in frame.

cue_material_break ON: plaza_lower grey block pavers vs plaza_light granite on flight+passage. The flight is invisible at every preset, so the material change is only read on the lit passage floor at depth (bright sheen patch at d2); at d10 the interior is a dark slit and the change is unreadable.

The scene signature (canopy shadow covering the flight, SUN_AZ_OFFSET 146.5 -> shadow azimuth 0deg along +X) is conflated with trench depth-darkness at judged poses - shadow and void merge into one black region. Distinct visible shadow lines are secondary: railing/canopy-column shadow stripes crossing the yellow head band at d2, parapet shadows on the rim.

At d2 the lit passage floor (L~140 sheen patch), retaining walls, covered-box headwall and even the east exit flight (x 30.2-36.6) are visible inside the trench - unambiguous depth. Moderate at d5; at d10 the interior collapses to a few dark rows.

cue_nosing ON (yellow 0.05m strip per step, color 0.85/0.72/0.10) but the flight is self-occluded at all 9 presets - the strips contribute ZERO pixels to any judged cut (verified: no yellow detected in the stair region; the only in-frame yellows are the tactile bands and the road median lines at x~18). They appear only in aux views (under_canopy: low-contrast olive lines inside the shadow - the intended signature).

Statutory stair-head warning band (0.60m deep, 0.30m setback, x -0.9..-0.3) is UNCONDITIONAL (bound to hazard_stairs, not cue_tactile) - present even in the cue-OFF arm. Dominant at mid poses: 14.5% of frame at h0.3_d2 (rows 535-692), rows 353-478 at h0.3_d5, ~10-row far band at h0.3_d10. Decorrelating twin: entrance band at x -6.0..-5.4 (NO drop behind it) crosses the near field in d10 cuts. At h0.9_d2 only the last 8 rows survive at frame bottom; at h1.8_d2 it is entirely below frame.

Statutory handrails (0.85m, one pipe/side) on the flight + split perimeter guardrail (0.9m on 0.15m parapet, y=+-1.65, running x 0..36.6). Visible in every preset - full frames at d2, thin (2-4px) but present receding lines at d10. The most persistent above-ground cue.

0.15m parapet upstand rims the trench (dark brick, visible flanking the pit at d2/d5). Beyond it, the GT-79 street kerbs (150mm registered linear drops at x 7.80/13.80) show as cream kerb lines across the frame at h0.9/h1.8. At h0.3 the parapet compresses to a few rows and kerb faces are edge-on.
Hedge bands (x -12..6.5 south verge, 32.5..36.5 east) and verge weeds are deliberately placed off the hazard (GT-71 doctrine); grass tufts on pavers are noise. No vegetation marks the drop.
No water in scene.

Blue 지하보도/UNDERPASS panel (post-mounted at head, y+2.6) + blank navy lintel band on the canopy west columns identify the underpass: ~1.7-4.3k blue-sign px from d5 out, but only ~10px at h0.3_d2 (above frame top at close range). Road centre/median/edge lines beyond the pit are visible at h0.9/h1.8 but belong to the street, not the drop.
Semi-gloss pit walls and a sheen patch on the passage floor contrast with matte pavers at d2/d5; unresolvable at d10.

Canopy columns (r=0.13) flank the void in every cut; railing frames, parapet end piers and the dark portal headwall (h 0.90) give a redundant structural silhouette even when the pit area shrinks to <5% of frame at d10.

shortcut_risks: Yellow band => drop: the statutory head band is unconditional and hugs the void in every arm; the entrance band (x -6, no drop) decorrelates only partially since both bands sit in the same corridor and only the head band touches a black region
Railing + dark void co-occurrence: every railing in the judged corridor guards this one trench

Very-dark-region => drop: canopy shadow and trench depth are visually merged, so the model can score on 'black blob on bright pavers' without reading geometry (sceneN1 is the cross-scene counter-negative, but within s16 all large dark blobs are hazard)
Underpass-prior: blue sign + twin canopy columns + portal band always co-occur with the drop
Fixed composition: edge always centered, dead ahead, at 3 known distances in the judged presets
suggestions: Age the statutory head tactile band: wear/soiling albedo patches and a few chipped dots (ubiquitous on real Korean tactile paving) so saturated-clean-yellow alone cannot carry the detection

Verify the prescribed canopy drip-stain band and rim joint weathering actually issue at the stair shoulder - a color-independent local edge texture that would survive at h0.3_d10 where the head band compresses to ~10 rows
Add tone variation to the passage floor (existing granite role, darker grout/wear zones) so far-side depth is not a single uniform bright patch at d2
Lean on the existing decorrelated dark features (manhole at -3.9/-0.8, utility-cut patch) - one more asphalt patch family member on the west walk would further break 'dark = pit' without new props

scenes.drop_type: T21 levee-bank contrast pair: 3.2m grass bank at 1:2 from crest x=0 (z=0) down to terrace z=-3.2; descended by (a) unrailed 20x0.16 concrete flight cutting straight through and (b) 25.6m diagonal ramp at 12.5% (yaw 75.5deg) with only a 0.15m river-side kerb - both declared below-code realities. Registered edge: levee_crest at x=0.
scenes.drop_summary: The designed trap scene: at robot height the sight line grazing the crest skips the entire bank/stairs/terrace band and near turf reads as one continuous plane with the far grass. No rail, no tactile, no nosing, no upstand beyond a 0.05m cope. Local evidence at h0.9+ is a single low-contrast concrete-to-grass boundary; at h0.3_d10 the whole river valley (bank to far waterline, ~100m) is invisible.

cues.notes: Crest line exists only where the concrete entry spur ends: spur L~126-128 vs grass L~105-113 (dL~20, Michelson ~0.08) at row ~545 in h0.9_d5. At h0.3 the boundary is grass-on-grass - no measurable luminance or hue step at the crest at all (row profile smooth through the crest rows).

Across the edge the surface is turf -> (hidden bank grass) -> terrace grass: the same texture family on both sides, which IS the trap. The real texture changes (pavers->asphalt->verge turf, and the concrete spurs) all lie BEFORE the edge along the approach, teaching position priors, not edge evidence.
Noon sun; no cast shadow marks the crest. Tree/bench/bridge-pier shadows are all off-edge (bridge shadow lies on the water).

Depth is visible but DISGUISED: terrace grass beyond the hidden band merges seamlessly with crest turf into one green band. The terrace promenade resolves as a distinct grey band only at h1.8_d2 (rows 747-960, L~126-134), h1.8_d5 and partially h0.9_d2 - elsewhere it is occluded by the crest. At h0.3_d10 the grazing ray lands ~100m out on far-bank grounds: the entire valley contributes zero pixels.
cue_nosing False; flight would be self-occluded at judged poses anyway.
cue_tactile False - not customary for river works; code path reserved only.
Unrailed by Han-river custom (declared below-code reality #1); cue_railing False. No fence prims at the crest or flight.

0.05m crest cope (x -0.20..0.05, opens at the spurs) shows as a thin dark cap flanking the spur end at h0.9/h1.8 (2-4px); the ramp's 0.15m river-side kerb on its 1.5m revetment is off-axis left and rarely resolvable in presets. Neither reads as a warning at h0.3.

Grass IS both sides of the edge, so vegetation marks the corridor, not the line. The one genuine vegetation depth hint: waterline silver-grass/reed stalks (culm r 0.006, on the measured waterline) poke above the crest sight line at d2 with hidden bases.

The broad river is the strongest surviving evidence at most poses: water+context ~12.6% of frame at h0.3_d2, 9-18% at h0.9/h1.8 (rough 0.18, pier reflections). But it thins to a ~20-row sliver at h0.3_d5 and is FULLY occluded at h0.3_d10 (crest-grazing ray overshoots the 72m water extent). It signals riverbank context, not the edge row.

White bike-road edge lines cross the near corridor 3-7m before the crest (approach prior, decorrelated from the edge itself). The km-marker blue panel (14.9,-4.6, top z=-1.0) and the terrace streetlight rise from below the crest with occluded bases - an indirect hidden-level hint, clearly visible at d2/d5.
Water specular (bridge piers mirrored at rough 0.18) is the only specular event; nothing at the crest itself.

Streetlight pole (h 4.6 from terrace, crossing the crest line vertically) + km-sign + reed stalks break the crest horizon with hidden bases; ramp batter/cheek shows as a dark wedge at frame left from h0.9 up; bridge deck + 4 far towers give strong 'river valley' context. At h0.3_d10 this reduces to one thin pole.

shortcut_risks: Water-as-proxy: 'river/reeds in frame => drop ahead' - the model can fire on context without localizing the crest; conversely at h0.3_d10 the water is gone and nothing replaces it
'Concrete slab ending in grass => edge': the spur-end boundary is the only local cue at h0.9+, and removal (turf lapping the crest) would erase local evidence entirely
'Pole without a visible base => hidden level' - real cue but spuriously learnable as pole-detector

Scene-level position prior: fixed composition means the drop is always at a constant distance beyond the pavers->asphalt->verge sequence; a model can regress the edge from the road markings without seeing it
Green-band prior: 'horizontal grass band between road and water = bank edge somewhere inside it' - ambiguity the GT mask does not share
suggestions: Differential mowing (strongest, fully realistic): render the bank-face grass taller/rougher than the crest verge turf - real levee crowns are mowed, slopes less so; a ragged 5-10cm fringe at x=0 would silhouette the crest even at h0.3 grazing, the exact pose where the scene is currently blind
Weather the crest cope (dirt/lichen darkening of the 0.05m cap) so a continuous thin dark line marks the crest at h0.9+ without moving any frozen geometry
Worn-earth patches at the stair and ramp heads where foot traffic converges (bare-soil wear is universal at unrailed levee stairs) - a local albedo/texture cue on the walked line
Continue the existing streetlight family along the terrace promenade at its real spacing so a hidden-base pole sits near frame center at every judged distance, not just d2/d5
Give crest turf and terrace grass slightly different tone/blade scale (crown turf vs floodplain meadow - botanically true) so the false green continuity breaks at h0.9 without a hard line

scenes.drop_type: Beach access revetment + flight: flush 2.560m granite seaward revetment at x=0 (no upstand; 0.35m coping course) between promenade z=0 and sand z=-2.56; a straight 16x0.160 granite flight (6m clear, tread 0.32, slope 26.6deg) cut through it, flanked by 0.12m stringer cheeks. Registered edge: revetment_edge at x=0.
scenes.drop_summary: The flight is invisible in ALL 9 presets (self-occluded behind the rim at h0.3/h0.9; below the -10deg frame at h1.8_d2; under the sight envelope at h1.8 d5/d10). The drop is evidenced by the dark coping bar at the edge, the sand field beyond (when not self-occluded), and the sea band - at h0.3_d5/d10 the sand disappears and everything reduces to a <=8-row dark line against the sea horizon.

cues.notes: Dark coping course (x -0.35..0) renders L~99-104 (neutral 99/101/104) vs promenade pavers L~182-186 and sand L~190-201: a -85..-94 step over 4 rows (Michelson 0.30-0.45). ~24 rows at h0.9_d5, ~8 rows at h0.3_d5, but collapses to ~2 rows at h0.3_d10 where it merges with the paver/sea junction; at h1.8_d2 the edge (42deg depression) is below the frame - zero drop-edge pixels in that cut.

Granite -> sand across the edge, the scene's core statement. Sand (tan-mask) frame fraction: h0.3: 10.6%/0.04%/0.05% (d2/d5/d10 - self-occluded beyond d2); h0.9: 51.4%/13.9%/1.6%; h1.8: 59%/37%/12%. At h1.8_d2 the frame is 100% far-field sand+sea with no pavers at all (near field below frame), so the CHANGE itself is out of frame.
No cast shadow at the revetment base: sand runs bright (199/187/159) right up to the coping band - the dark bar is material, not shadow. Noon geometry leaves no shading event at the edge.

Beach apron, damp-sand band, tapered surf lines and sea read below/beyond the edge at h0.9/h1.8 and at h0.3_d2 (sand rows 383-692). Fully self-occluded at h0.3_d5/d10 - the 2.56m drop hides its own floor, leaving only sea.
RF-5 applied-strip nosing cancelled (cue_nosing False); the flight is self-occluded at every preset regardless.

Deliberately decorrelated: yellow guide strip + tan band are 12m LANDWARD (x -13.4..-12.2), behind all preset cameras - yellow fraction is 0.0000 in all 9 judged cuts. The drop edge carries no tactile.
cue_railing False; open revetment and unguarded flight (mid-rail cancelled by 6.1 ruling).

The revetment edge itself is flush (no upstand - the declared reality). Only the flight's stringer cheeks (0.12m, outside the 6m walked width) rise above deck; their oblique haunches are the sole above-deck geometry.
Kerbed planting beds are landward (x -17.6..-13.4), out of every judged frame.

Sea occupies 17-30% of EVERY preset frame (blue-mask), with 4 tapered breaker lines, damp-sand/swash events and a true horizon (plate sized to <0.5 row of the eye-line). Persistent, but it sits beyond the beach - it labels 'coast', not the edge row; at h0.3_d10 the paver/sea junction and the collapsed coping line are nearly the same rows.
Nothing signed in judged frames (guide strip is landward and behind camera).

Sea specular deliberately capped (rough 0.38, spec 0.42, no sun-glint path by design); sand and granite matte. Sea/sky luminance separation is held (~26% at horizon band) but there is no specular event at the drop edge.

Two dark cheek-haunch trapezoids (~30px tall at d10) flank the flight cut on the horizon line - the only positive-geometry signature of the stair; suspension bridge (left) and headland (right) are far context. At h1.8_d2 no near-field geometry is in frame.

shortcut_risks: 'Uniform dark horizontal bar across pavement => drop edge': the coping course is the only edge-localizing cue once sand self-occludes (h0.3_d5/d10); a coping recolored to promenade granite would make the drop invisible at robot height
'Blue above grey => waterfront edge at the junction row': at h0.3_d10 the paver/sea adjacency does localize the edge - a model can learn horizon-adjacency instead of the coping
'Sand texture in frame => drop': sand visibility is pose-gated, teaching a height-dependent proxy rather than edge evidence
'Symmetric dark trapezoid pair => stair cut' - the haunches are a unique, tiny signature that could be memorized
Fixed composition prior: edge dead-ahead at 3 fixed distances in judged cuts
suggestions: Break the coping's constant luminance with prescribed-style weathering: salt efflorescence patches (row spec already caps albedo at 0.30) plus damp/water staining segments, so the edge line is a textured band, not a learnable uniform bar

scenes.drop_type: stair_edge, snow-buried (condition variant C1)
scenes.drop_summary: Straight 12-step flight (riser 0.17 / tread 0.30, width 2.5 m), drop 2.04 m starting at x=0; 5 cm snow layer (front flush with riser, 45-deg 30 mm chamfer) bridges treads into one white slope. Overcast HDRI (dome 800) + soft sun elev 28 deg / 420 intensity: deliberately low-contrast. Approach carries a 1.0 m brown cleared-snow wear lane ending 0.10 m before the edge; one-sided white pipe railing (+Y); tactile and yellow nosing built but buried; brick-toned stringers proud 20 mm flank the mouth.

cues.notes: Snow-on-snow arris draws almost no line. Measured pure-snow strip across the edge: Michelson 0.106 at h0.9_d5 (near footprint snow L 0.83 vs far content 0.67, and part of that step is far-side hedge darkening, not the arris), only 0.024 at h1.8_d10. At the whole h0.3 row the crest line is invisible (grazing tangent hides the far side entirely). The GT-119 chamfer re-cut succeeded: no cantilever/shadow-slot artifact remains, so the honest edge signal is near zero by design.

Near terrace snow is footprint-dimpled (trace_steps + skin, local sd 0.05-0.08); the first visible far surface is smoother lower-ground snow with a faint paving grid. Analytic tangent: far ground first visible at x=+12 m (h0.9_d5), +11.7 m (h1.8_d10), never nearer than 16-82 m at the h0.3 row - so the texture pair is present only h0.9_d2/d5 and h1.8 row, and always separated by an image gap, not adjacent.

Signature precondition: overcast dome + soft low sun azimuthed so no tread shadows form (checked: no step shading in any preset). The only cast shadows are lamp poles crossing the wear lane at x<0 - decorrelated from the drop.

At h0.9_d5/h1.8 rows: lower-ground snow band from x~12 m, dark evergreen hedge tops (L~0.1-0.2) cut by the edge at frame flanks, building C base occluded (plinth at z=-2.04). At h0.3 row the lower ground is never visible (tangent ground intercept 16/38/82 m at d2/d5/d10); only the building-base cutoff remains, which is far too subtle to read a 2.04 m drop.

Yellow band (0.85,0.72,0.10) built on all 12 treads but fully buried under the 5 cm snow; only a ~6 mm front face at each riser plane stays exposed (self-check [4] note), visible only from lower_lookback. Exposed in the snow_cover=False twin - the twin arm is the only place this cue trains.
Statutory 300-grid dot pavers at x -0.9..-0.3 (proud 4 mm) are the scene signature burial: 5 cm snow covers them completely; zero screen contribution in all judged presets. Twin exposes them.

One-sided (+Y/left) white pipe railing with marble-capped head wall; its descending diagonal below the ground line is THE dominant drop cue at every preset. At h0.3_d10 it survives only as a white silhouette against the brick facade (local contrast vs brick L 0.49 vs 0.27, sd 0.24) that plausibly reads as a leaning ladder - present but semantically ambiguous.

Exposed concrete/brick stringer tops (proud 20 mm over the bank snow, y 1.20-1.45 both sides) emerge as two small tan wedges flanking the stair mouth and sink within ~1 m (verified by crop zoom at h0.9_d5 px~1360,520 and mirrored left). Tiny (a few hundred px at d5, ~10 px at d10) but they are the only non-railing marker of the mouth.

Dark trimmed-hedge rows on the lower ground (perpendicular rows x 11.4-12.1, tops z~-1.19) appear as dark bands just beyond the crest at frame flanks in h0.9_d5/h1.8 presets - a depth marker, not an edge marker. Upper-terrace hedge rows flank the approach without touching the edge.
No water in this scene (winter/snow).
cue_sign=False. A generic blue park signpost (dressing, x=-3.2,y=-3.4) and a marker pole exist on the terrace but do not mark the edge; no pavement markings.
Snow rough 0.95 / spec 0.1 both sides of the edge; railing metal glints do not localize the drop.

The gestalt that carries the h0.9/h1.8 rows: railing dipping below the ground line + hedge/bench/house/building bases cut by the crest. At h0.3 only the building-base cutoff and the ambiguous railing silhouette remain; the terrain silhouette itself is a featureless white plane.

shortcut_risks: white one-sided railing => drop: the railing is the only strong cue in all 9 presets; cue_railing=False ablation exists as a toggle but is not in the render mix

brown cleared wear lane terminating => drop directly beyond: lane stops 0.10 m before the edge and its termination boundary is the strongest luminance edge in the scene (Michelson 0.27-0.47 vs 0.02-0.11 for the true edge)
texture split shortcut: footprint-dimpled snow = near/safe plane, smooth grid-marked snow = lower plane - the texture pair is perfectly correlated with the level split
scene-level prior: overcast whiteout + snow scene => positive GT (no in-scene negative region; hazard_stairs=False / snow_cover=False twins must enter the corpus to break it)
paired tan stringer wedges flanking a lane end => stair mouth (unique, repeated arrangement)
suggestions: Wind-scour bald patch: locally thin the snow (thickness ~0.01-0.02) over 1-2 tread noses in a 0.3-0.5 m y-band mid-flight so a dark concrete nosing arc peeks through - realistic on a used stair, gives an honest, partial edge_line at h0.9+ without collapsing the concealment identity

Continue the trampled trace DOWN the flight: compressed-snow footprint depressions on the buried tread line (same trace_steps vocabulary, albedo x0.9) - periodic ridge shading turns the white slope into a weakly-stepped slope, a legitimate non-railing cue
Crest settling line: a 2-3 cm albedo x0.93 band (or 1-2 deg top tilt of the NoseTop wedge) along x=0 - snow sags over an unsupported arris in reality; restores a faint true-edge line at h0.9/h1.8

Decorrelate lane termination: extend the cleared lane onto the lower ground beyond the stair foot (people keep walking), and/or end a second cleared spur harmlessly at the bench so 'lane ends' stops predicting 'drop'
Put the existing toggles into the training mix: render cue_railing=False and snow_cover=False arms so railing<->drop and whiteout<->positive decorrelate without new geometry

Optional lighting arm: one dome-rotation/sun-elev ~20 deg raking variant (existing [ ] sweep knob) that gives the chamfered ridges genuine relief at h0.3 - diversity for shadow_line without abandoning the overcast signature arm

scenes.drop_type: stair_edge, leaf-buried (condition variant C2)
scenes.drop_summary: Park stone stair, 14 steps (riser 0.16 / tread 0.34, width 2.6 m), drop 2.24 m from x=0. Leaf mound B crests at x=-0.25, z=+0.20 (above the approach!), fully burying steps 1-3; mound C center-fills steps 4-7; steps 8-14 exposed but hidden behind the crest from upstream. Sunny (sun elev 42 deg); dark-gray one-sided railing is the designed sole cue over the buried run; green trimmed hedge closes the lower walk at x~21.8.

cues.notes: The 'edge' is the leaf-mound crest silhouette, an irregular soft ridge. At h0.9_d5 crest-vs-lawn Michelson 0.13 (leaf L 0.31 vs lawn 0.34), mostly chromatic (brown vs green). At h0.3_d10 the crest cuts against SKY (leaf 0.32 vs sky 0.79) - a strong line with the wrong semantics: it reads as an uphill leaf bank, not a 2.24 m drop.

Leaf mass -> green lawn + tan walk (L 0.58) with visible 2.4 m-pitch contraction joints, at h0.9_d2/d5 and h1.8 row. Analytic tangent over the crest: lower ground first visible at x=+5.9 (h0.9_d2), +16.3 (h0.9_d5), +14.6 (h1.8_d10); NEVER at the h0.3 row (intercept 42 m+, past the hedge) and not at h0.9_d10 (34 m). Warning: a full-width salmon-pink speckled band (RGB ~0.47,0.33,0.25; B-channel +0.06-0.08 vs leaves) sits in the crest compression zone in every upstream preset - the leaf_ground underlayer (tint 0.94,0.60,0.41) surfacing mip-averaged at grazing; it is a synthetic tell, not a real material boundary.

Sun az ~205 throws the crest's own cast shadow downhill, hidden behind the crest from upstream. Useful shadow evidence exists only obliquely (rail_cue: baluster shadows drape and bend down the mound) plus leaf-card micro-shadows that read as texture, not as an edge.

h0.9_d2 and h1.8_d2/d5: lower walk, bollard-lamp pair, lawn, bench and pergola appear below the crest line; at h1.8_d2 the tangent clears the mound entirely so the whole pit interior (leaf ramp + exposed steps 8-14) is directly visible. h0.9_d5 keeps only a compressed sliver (ground x 16.3-21.8). At the h0.3 row nothing below the crest is visible; the only depth inference is the hedge line standing abnormally close above the leaf texture (and at h0.3_d10 even the hedge drops below the tangent, leaving near-empty sky).
cue_nosing=False - anti-slip strips are not the practice on worn park stone (code path reserved).
cue_tactile=False - below installation threshold for a park dirt path (spec 12.4, p=0.24).

Single dark-gray (0.14) pipe rail, one side: its descending diagonal is the designed only-cue over the buried run and reads in every preset (at h0.3_d10 as a dark gate-like frame mid-field whose far half sinks). At h0.3_d2 only the upper section is in frame top-left and the descent is partly out of frame - the weakest case. Baluster feet are buried in the leaf mass, which slightly softens the 'goes below ground' reading.

Stone coping (0.12 proud of the nosing line, both flanks, ext 0.25 upstream) reads only as two small gray end-blocks flanking the crest at h0.9/h1.8; the descending coping body is buried under the flank leaf drifts.

Green trimmed-hedge line + green lawn are the chromatic far side; the hedge 'closes' the walk at x~21.8, so its unusual closeness above the crest is the real depth tell at h0.3_d2. It marks the horizon rather than the edge; at h0.3_d10 the hedge falls below the crest tangent and disappears, removing even this.
No water.
No signs or markings (park lamps, bins, bench, pergola only); walk joints are structural, not markings.
Leaves rough 0.90, walk and lawn matte; no gloss boundary at the crest. The pink crest band is a chroma artifact, not specular.

Railing diagonal aside: pergola posts, lower bench, bollard lamps and tree trunks rise base-cut from behind the crest at h0.9/h1.8. At h0.3 the mound's own convex silhouette actively signals 'uphill bank' - a counter-cue.

shortcut_risks: dark railing diagonal => drop: designed as the sole cue over the buried run; 100% co-occurrence in-scene (cue_railing=False toggle exists but is not rendered into the mix)

dense leaf carpet => positive GT: the leaf layer IS the burial device, so leaf texture itself predicts the label; the corpus has no leaf-carpet-on-flat negative (leaf_cover=False twin is bare stairs - still positive)
salmon-pink speckled band at the texture horizon => drop: leaf_ground underlayer tint surfacing mip-blurred at the crest compression zone in every upstream preset - purely synthetic correlate
green trimmed-hedge blob row directly above leaf texture => drop (hedge closes the walk exactly behind the pit)
leaf field flanked by two gray stone blocks => stair mouth
suggestions: Kill the pink crest band: extend 3D-card cover over the crest strip (one more seam rect straddling x -0.4..+0.3, cover ~0.20, appended so existing scatter stays bit-identical) or damp the leaf_tex_tint B channel - the underlayer must not surface at the silhouette where it is a label-correlated artifact

Kick-through notch: lower mound B's crest 2-3 cm in one ~0.4 m y-notch (people kick leaves at a stair head) exposing one dark stone nosing sliver + shadow slot - an honest partial edge_line visible from h0.9 that diversifies away from the railing
Expose 0.3-0.5 m of coping shoulder above the leaf line on one flank (rake the drift locally) - a real curb cue that survives the h0.3 row where everything else dies
Compressed trample swale: a 0.4 m wide, albedo x0.85 depression along y~0 across mound A/B converging on the crest - implies passage and gives a converging texture cue terminating at the drop

Render cue_railing=False and leaf_cover=False arms into the training mix to break railing<->drop and leaf<->positive; additionally lay a same-vocabulary leaf carpet on a flat stretch of the LOWER walk (already partially there, x to 7.76) extended past the pit so 'leaf field' appears without a drop beneath it in the same scene
At h1.8_d2 the whole pit interior is visible - keep that preset weighted in training; it is the one upstream view where the true geometry (progressive exposure) teaches the right feature

scenes.drop_type: stair_edge, wet-mirror merged (condition variant C4)
scenes.drop_summary: Wide granite civic stair, 14 steps (riser 0.15 / tread 0.35, width 6.0 m), drop 2.10 m from x=0. Rain-wet material layer: tread patch tiers rough 0.10/0.20/0.35 with 30-50% albedo darkening, transparent water films (opacity 0.22) and plaza pools; overcast sunless dome (1150) so specular faces mirror a uniform sky and step edges merge. Yellow dot tactile at a deliberately non-compliant 1.0 m setback; stainless railings on BOTH cheek bands; lower plaza with planters, lamps, sculpture, colonnade.

cues.notes: No dedicated arris line (nosing off, wet film runs to the edge). The head line exists as a tone step: across-edge Michelson 0.109 at h0.9_d5 (near crackle strip L 0.477 vs far plaza 0.383) and 0.109 at h0.3_d2. At h0.3_d5/d10 it compresses to 1-2 px and the visible 'line' is really the tactile band.

Near side = stone_flag crackle (luminance sd 0.051), far lower plaza = smooth wet sheet (sd 0.013): a 4:1 texture-energy step co-located with the level change, readable at h0.9/h1.8 rows and h0.3_d2. At h0.3_d5/d10 the far ground is occluded (tangent intercept 35/70 m) - what shows above the tactile is stylobate/plinth zone and the dark lower pool.
Sunless overcast profile is the scene precondition (hard shadows would revive the edges); no shadow cues anywhere.

h0.9_d2 sees the lower plaza from x~4.7 (virtually the stair foot); h1.8_d2 tangent grazes the arris so the whole flight is visible; h0.9_d5 / h1.8_d5-d10 show the far plaza from 11.7-23.4 m with planter walls, lamp bases, sculpture monolith and colonnade all rising base-cut from below the edge line. At the h0.3 row the far ground vanishes (intercepts 14/35/70 m) leaving only base-cut verticals and the dark pool zone.
cue_nosing=False by design - nosing paint would defeat the edge-merge feature; reserved as an ablation arm.

Yellow dot pavers (realistically non-compliant 1.0 m setback, 0.6 m deep, full 6 m width): L 0.75-0.78 vs surrounding plaza 0.29-0.48 - the highest-contrast object in every preset. Still identifiable at h0.3_d10 as an ~8 px full-width line (L 0.353, sd 0.136, between 0.27/0.43 neighbors). Dominant to the point of being the scene's main shortcut vector.

Stainless rails on BOTH cheek bands; the symmetric double descending diagonal reads at h0.9/h1.8 rows and at h0.3_d5/d10; at h0.3_d2 the rails sit at/outside the frame edges and the descent gestalt is largely lost.
Stone cheek bands proud 60 mm flank the head but read as thin shoulders only near d2/d5 at h0.9+; planter curbs on both plazas are off-corridor context rather than edge markers.

Grass banks flanking the stair are outside the cheek bands and essentially invisible from upstream presets (clearly green only in lower_lookback); planter shrubs/boulders at frame edges are context. Effectively a non-cue upstream.

Tread films are occluded at all 9 upstream presets (treads geometrically hidden). What shows: the upper dark wet sheet (L 0.29 vs plaza 0.48) abutting the tactile band at h0.9/h1.8 rows and h0.3_d2, and the lower-plaza pool as the dark zone just beyond the edge (it is what darkens the far band at h0.3_d10). Films correctly transparent (opacity 0.22) per the R-2 ruling.
cue_sign=False; bollard row with white reflective bands at x=-6 is entrance furniture behind most preset eyes, not an edge marking.

The scene signature: wet tiers (rough 0.10-0.35) mirror the uniform overcast sky, erasing riser shading (edge merge) and producing a sheen gradient; the near-crackle-sheen vs far-smooth-mirror boundary is co-located with the edge and strongest at grazing (h0.3) where the far plaza reads as one bright sheet. Double-edged: it both IS the concealment and provides the gloss-boundary evidence.

Twin rails dipping below the plaza line + base-cut verticals (colonnade columns, plaza lamps, monolith, planter walls) at h0.9/h1.8; at h0.3 the verticals' base-cut remains readable while the rail diagonals compress (fully so at d2).

shortcut_risks: yellow dot band => drop 1 m ahead: 100% within-scene co-occurrence and the highest-contrast object in every frame; needs cue_tactile=False arms and corpus scenes where tactile precedes non-drop transitions (crossings, platform doors) to stay honest
dark wet sheet adjacent to bright yellow band => edge (the upper sheet x -4.8..-1.4 abuts the tactile in every view)
smooth+bright (or pool-dark) low-texture far field above a crackle band => drop: the texture-energy step is perfectly level-correlated in-scene
symmetric twin stainless diagonals => stair pit
scene-level prior: sunless flat light + wet gloss => positive GT (wet_surface=False and hazard_stairs=False twins must appear in the training mix)
suggestions: Dry-arris strip: give a 2-3 cm band along x=0 the damp tier (rough 0.40, damp_tint) instead of strong-wet - an unsupported edge drains and dries first in reality, restoring a thin honest roughness/tone line at the head visible from h0.9 without breaking the merge signature on the treads
Decorrelate the dark sheet: move (or duplicate in one arm) a plaza water sheet to x -9..-7 so 'dark sheet' also occurs far from any edge; the existing gully sites make it plausible
Put the existing ablation arms into the mix: cue_tactile=False, cue_nosing=True, wet_surface=False - they are already wired as toggles and directly break the three strongest in-scene correlations
Dome Z-rotation arms (existing [ ] sweep) to vary the overcast luminance-gradient direction so 'bright sheet at the top of frame' is not a fixed positive signature
Keep h1.8_d2 (whole flight visible, riser shading readable through the film) weighted in training as the geometry-teaching upstream view
